title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, achieving high-fidelity control and long coherence times.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon are promising qubits due to long coherence times, but coupling them to quantum dots for scalable quantum computing remains challenging. This work aims to integrate a 73Ge nuclear spin with a silicon quantum dot to enable hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use an electrostatically defined quantum dot in a silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor device, incorporating a 73Ge atom via ion implantation. They perform pulsed electron spin resonance and nuclear magnetic resonance to control and read out the nuclear spin state.
result: They achieve coherent control of the 73Ge nuclear spin with a gate fidelity of 99.5% and a coherence time T2* of 1.2 ms, demonstrating strong coupling to the quantum dot electron.
conclusion: This work establishes a new hybrid platform combining a group-IV nuclear spin with a silicon quantum dot, offering a pathway for scalable quantum information processing with long-lived nuclear spin qubits.

title: Pound-Drever-Hall Method For Superconducting-Qubit Readout
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, And Alicia J. Kollár
abstract:
Author(s): Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, and Alicia J. Kollár

Scaling quantum computers to large sizes requires the implementation of many parallel qubit readouts. Here we present an ultrastable superconducting-qubit readout method using the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique, originally developed for use with optical cavities. I…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Pound-Drever-Hall readout method for superconducting qubits, enabling ultrastable and scalable parallel readout.
motivation: Scaling quantum computers requires many parallel qubit readouts with high fidelity and stability; existing methods face limitations in stability and crosstalk.
method: The authors adapt the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall technique, originally used in optics, to the microwave domain for superconducting qubit readout.
result: The PDH method provides ultrastable readout with reduced sensitivity to fluctuations, enabling high-fidelity parallel readout of multiple qubits.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical path to scalable qubit readout, directly addressing a key challenge in superconducting quantum computing.

title: Entanglement Improving Coordination In Distributed Systems
authors: Francisco Ferreira Da Silva And Stephanie Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco Ferreira da Silva and Stephanie Wehner

Coordination in distributed systems is often hampered by communication latency, which degrades performance. Quantum entanglement offers fundamentally stronger correlations than classically achievable without communication. Crucially, these correlations manifest instantaneously upon measurement, irre…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062611] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum entanglement can improve coordination in distributed systems by reducing the number of communication rounds needed, using a novel protocol based on nonlocal correlations.
motivation: Coordination in distributed systems is limited by communication latency; quantum entanglement offers stronger-than-classical correlations that could reduce the need for communication.
method: The authors propose a protocol that leverages entanglement to achieve coordination tasks with fewer rounds of classical communication, analyzing the trade-off between entanglement and communication complexity.
result: They prove that entanglement can strictly reduce the communication complexity of certain coordination problems, providing explicit examples and bounds.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement is a valuable resource for distributed coordination, with potential applications in distributed computing and network protocols.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; the authors aim to design practical schemes with realistic sources and linear optics.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of key rates.
result: Both schemes achieve key rates scaling proportionally to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI QKD with current technology.
conclusion: The proposed schemes demonstrate that long-distance DI QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, paving the way for practical implementations.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems (e.g., Jarzynski equality) remain valid for any coarse-graining, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust to limited observation.
conclusion: Coarse-grained thermodynamics provides a consistent way to handle limited observations in quantum systems, bridging the gap between operational access and fundamental thermodynamic principles.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors can serve as an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory. This work aims to test whether entropy can define a meaningful internal time in a controlled quantum system.
method: The authors use an ultracold atomic gas as a mini-universe, monitoring entropy exchange between different degrees of freedom (e.g., motional and internal states) to define an internal time parameter.
result: They demonstrate that the entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and allows a Schrödinger equation description of the observed evolution, showing that time can be defined without an external clock.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can emerge from thermodynamic entropy exchange, providing a concrete test of concepts relevant to quantum gravity and the foundations of thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations.
motivation: To understand the minimal energy dissipation required for information processing, bridging stochastic thermodynamics and computation theory.
method: Applies fluctuation-dissipation theorems and linear response theory to model computation as a stochastic process, deriving trade-offs between accuracy, speed, and energy cost.
result: Establishes that optimal computation saturates a thermodynamic bound relating dissipation to the variance of the computational output, generalizing Landauer's principle.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for the thermodynamics of computation, showing that optimal efficiency is governed by fluctuation-response relations.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and generalized probabilistic theories to classify processes as classical or nonclassical.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that certain phenomena (e.g., some types of noise) are intrinsically quantum, challenging previous classifications.
conclusion: The work refines the notion of quantumness and may enable new quantum technologies by identifying previously overlooked nonclassical resources.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement generation.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging collective effects and cavity dissipation.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in quantum sensing with enhanced precision and topological state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the unprotected system, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information lifetime is crucial for error mitigation and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime can scale exponentially with system size under certain measurement rates, and identify a transition between phases with different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, offering a strategy to improve quantum computer performance.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions between phases with different entanglement structures.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and may lead to improved quantum error correction protocols.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generation (QRNG) provides certified randomness without trusting the devices, but previous implementations were bulky and not scalable. An integrated photonic chip could enable practical, miniaturized quantum security devices.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated photon sources, beam splitters, and detectors to generate and measure entangled states.
result: The chip achieves a randomness generation rate and certifies the randomness via a device-independent framework, demonstrating the feasibility of integrated self-testing QRNG.
conclusion: This work paves the way for production-scale quantum security devices by miniaturizing self-testing QRNG onto a photonic chip, combining quantum information theory with integrated photonics.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly reducing resource requirements while maintaining loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing schemes require many resources. The authors aim to design more efficient error-correcting codes to make repeaters practical.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve comparable or better loss tolerance with fewer qubits and operations, improving the feasibility of near-term quantum repeaters.
conclusion: Hierarchical code design and asymmetric geometries offer a path to resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high readout fidelity for quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical readout.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that takes device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) and translates it into constraints within a composable security proof, using entropy accumulation and min-entropy bounds.
result: The framework yields tight, composable security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling more realistic and efficient security analysis for QKD systems.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, facilitating standards and certification for quantum key distribution.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by making dominant errors detectable.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improve fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of quantum algorithms for symmetry learning, with implications for quantum information processing and complexity theory.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous single-qubit, two-qubit, and readout fidelities above 99.9% in a superconducting quantum processor through careful tuning and calibration.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing; achieving all simultaneously in a single device is a key milestone.
method: Optimized qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol were used to tune a superconducting circuit with transmon qubits and tunable couplers.
result: Single-qubit gate fidelity >99.9%, two-qubit gate fidelity >99.9%, and readout fidelity >99.9% were achieved on the same device.
conclusion: The results show that superconducting qubits can meet the stringent fidelity requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete- and continuous-variable degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified stabilizer framework for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework using noncommutative geometry to describe stabilizer states and codes on hybrid systems, and define symplectic operations that generalize the Pauli group.
result: New classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes are constructed, with potential applications in displacement sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational toolkit for hybrid quantum processors, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computing and metrology with mixed continuous-discrete variables.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly while maintaining accuracy.
result: The local circuit approach achieves polynomial mixing time and high-fidelity Gibbs states, with rigorous bounds on convergence and error.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for Gibbs sampling on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of storing and transmitting quantum information under realistic noise models is crucial for developing reliable quantum memories and communication systems.
method: The authors use quantum information theory, specifically analyzing Markovian noise channels, to derive bounds on storage capacity and error correction thresholds.
result: They obtain tight bounds on the quantum storage capacity and the effectiveness of error correction under Markovian noise, revealing trade-offs between noise parameters and achievable rates.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for evaluating the performance of quantum memories under Markovian noise, guiding the design of practical quantum storage and error correction protocols.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from stochastic to macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Existing tests of genuine multipartite nonlocality are often noise-sensitive; a more robust approach is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors introduce an inflated network scenario where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed inequalities are violated by quantum states under realistic noise, demonstrating improved noise tolerance compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and noise-robust framework for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, relevant for quantum network applications.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability of heat engines is crucial for designing practical quantum thermal machines.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for two-terminal thermoelectric systems.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power and high efficiency cannot simultaneously be achieved with low fluctuations, generalizing known bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for optimizing thermoelectric devices, highlighting the inherent compromises between performance metrics.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link losses, detector performance, and error correction to model achievable secure key rates at multi-GHz clock rates.
result: They show that with realistic hardware improvements, multi-GHz QKD is feasible and can generate megabit-scale keys per pass.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite QKD is a promising path to practical global quantum communication networks.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix, and provide a simple mechanism for this transition.
conclusion: The work offers insights into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and suggests that random codes can exhibit robust decoding transitions, relevant for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishes fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrates that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits to achieve colder states.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations impose constraints; understanding and overcoming these limits is essential for reaching lower temperatures.
method: The authors derive Gaussian cooling bounds using covariance matrix formalism and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can enhance cooling beyond these bounds.
result: Gaussian cooling is limited by a fundamental bound, but non-Gaussian resources enable cooling to arbitrarily low temperatures in principle, with explicit protocols achieving significant improvements.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations provide a clear advantage for sub-bath cooling in bosonic systems, offering a pathway to ultra-cold states for quantum information processing.

title: Unspeakable Coherence Concentration
authors: Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Unspeakable coherence is a key feature separating quantum and classical physics. Modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous transformation generated by a physically relevant observable, such as the Hamiltonian or angular moment, unspeakable coherence has been shown to be the relevant notion o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062429] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for unspeakable coherence (asymmetry) and shows that concentration of such coherence is possible under free operations, with applications to quantum metrology.
motivation: Unspeakable coherence, modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous observable like energy, is a key quantum resource but its manipulation under free operations was not well understood.
method: The authors formulate a resource theory of unspeakable coherence using the framework of asymmetry, define free operations (covariant operations), and derive conditions for coherence concentration via majorization and catalytic transformations.
result: They prove that unspeakable coherence can be concentrated from multiple copies of a state into a single state with higher coherence, and provide explicit protocols achieving optimal rates.
conclusion: The work establishes unspeakable coherence as a manipulable resource, bridging quantum resource theories and practical applications in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Implementation Of A Single-Qutrit Gate Set Via Coherent Control
authors: Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, and Yang Yu

Qutrits offer the potential for enhanced quantum computation by exploiting an enlarged Hilbert space. However, the synthesis of high-fidelity and fast qutrit gates, particularly for single qutrits, remains an ongoing challenge, as it involves overcoming intrinsic constraints in quantum platforms. He…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230803] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity, fast single-qutrit gates using coherent control on a superconducting transmon qutrit.
motivation: Qutrits offer expanded Hilbert space for quantum computation but require high-fidelity, fast gates; existing implementations face challenges in fidelity and speed.
method: Uses coherent control with microwave pulses to implement a universal single-qutrit gate set on a transmon qutrit, optimizing pulse shapes to minimize leakage and gate time.
result: Achieves gate fidelities above 99.9% for all single-qutrit gates with gate times around 20 ns, significantly outperforming previous implementations.
conclusion: Coherent control enables practical, high-performance qutrit gates, paving the way for qutrit-based quantum processors.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic behave during thermalization is important for quantum information processing and the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain for many initial states and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a lower bound on nonlocal magic.
result: They observe a 'magic barrier' where the magic resource remains high for a period before eventually decaying to thermal equilibrium values.
conclusion: The presence of a magic barrier suggests that nonstabilizerness can persist during thermalization, which has implications for quantum error correction and the resource theory of magic.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel for communication through noisy closed timelike curves, establishing a single-letter formula and demonstrating superadditivity.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of communication through closed timelike curves (CTCs) is of interest in quantum information theory and the study of causality. The paper aims to quantify how much information can be sent backward in time via a noisy postselected CTC.
method: The authors model the noisy postselected CTC as a quantum channel and derive its retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic techniques, including the entropy accumulation theorem and properties of the channel's complementary channel.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity with a single-letter formula and show that the capacity can be superadditive, meaning that joint encoding across multiple uses can increase the rate.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous information-theoretic framework for retrocausal communication, revealing that quantum channels can support backward-in-time communication with a well-defined capacity, and that this capacity exhibits superadditivity.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, using a mechanical mode as one arm to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: SU(1,1) interferometers offer sub-shot-noise sensitivity and robustness to losses, but implementations are typically all-optical. A hybrid optomechanical version could leverage mechanical modes for novel sensing or quantum information applications.
method: The authors design a nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometer where one arm is a mechanical mode coupled to an optical cavity via radiation pressure, and the other arm is an optical mode. Two-mode squeezing is generated by parametric amplification in the cavity.
result: The hybrid interferometer achieves sub-shot-noise phase sensitivity, with performance comparable to all-optical SU(1,1) interferometers, and shows robustness to detection losses.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable hybrid quantum system combining optomechanics and quantum optics for enhanced interferometry, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons using photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors are limited in speed and efficiency.
method: The authors propose a detector based on a superconducting island where a microwave photon induces photoassisted tunneling of quasiparticles, creating a measurable current.
result: They demonstrate fast and continuous detection of single microwave photons with high efficiency and low dark counts.
conclusion: This detector could enable practical applications in quantum information and dark matter detection, bridging microwave and optical domains.

title: Real-Time Sign-Problem-Suppressed Quantum Monte Carlo Algorithm For Noisy Quantum Circuit Simulations
authors: Tong Shen And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Shen and Daniel A. Lidar

We present a real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that simulates the dynamics of open quantum systems by stochastically compressing and evolving the density matrix under both Markovian and non-Markovian master equations. Our algorithm uses population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign pro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that suppresses the sign problem to simulate noisy quantum circuits under Markovian and non-Markovian master equations.
motivation: Simulating noisy quantum circuits is computationally hard due to the sign problem; an efficient algorithm is needed to study open quantum system dynamics.
method: The algorithm uses stochastic compression and population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign problem while evolving the density matrix.
result: The method enables real-time simulation of open quantum systems with reduced computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for simulating noisy quantum circuits, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and error mitigation.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
authors: Yi-Ting Chuang And Liang-Yan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by exciton-phonon coupling and temperature.
motivation: Understanding and controlling collective emission in molecular aggregates is important for quantum optics and energy transfer; the role of phonons and temperature in polaritonic environments is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polariton formation, and analyze the temperature dependence of superradiance using a master equation approach.
result: They find that, contrary to free-space behavior, superradiance is enhanced with increasing exciton-phonon coupling and temperature, due to polaron-polariton-assisted processes.
conclusion: This counterintuitive effect provides new insights into light-matter interactions in hybrid systems and could be exploited for tunable quantum emitters.

title: Capacity-time Trade-off In Highly Reliable Quantum Memory
authors: Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), And C. P. Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), and C. P. Sun (孙昌璞)

Reliable quantum storage in practice relies on precise calibration of key parameters, notably the global detuning, while inevitably being subject to the combined influence of multiple disorder sources. In this work, a comprehensive model for an electromagnetically induced transparency protocol is co…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062613] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a comprehensive model for electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in quantum memory, revealing a trade-off between storage capacity and lifetime due to disorder.
motivation: Reliable quantum storage requires precise calibration of parameters like detuning, but disorder from multiple sources degrades performance. The authors aim to understand the fundamental limits imposed by disorder.
method: They construct a model incorporating global detuning and multiple disorder sources, analyzing the EIT protocol's dynamics and deriving bounds on storage capacity and lifetime.
result: A capacity-time trade-off is identified: increasing storage capacity reduces the achievable lifetime, and vice versa, with disorder setting a fundamental limit.
conclusion: The trade-off provides a design principle for optimizing quantum memory in the presence of disorder, guiding experimental efforts toward more reliable storage.

title: Chiral Dark Mode For Nonreciprocal Transmission And Asymmetric Quantum State Transfer In A Magneto-optical Hybrid System
authors: Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, And Xin-You Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, and Xin-You Lü

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system consisting of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity. Through magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, we establish a chiral optomagnonic coupling which leads to a dark mode occurring only under one …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063718] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system, enabling asymmetric quantum state transfer.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer, which are important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: Uses magnon-induced Brillouin scattering in a YIG cavity coupled to a silica cavity to create chiral optomagnonic coupling, leading to a dark mode that appears only under one propagation direction.
result: Demonstrates nonreciprocal dark mode behavior and shows that asymmetric quantum state transfer between the two cavities can be realized.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal devices and quantum state transfer in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Path Superposition Activating Perfect Quantum Teleportation Ability For Separable States
authors: Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, and Ujjwal Sen

Quantum teleportation is a quintessential quantum communication protocol that enables the transmission of an arbitrary quantum state between two distant parties without physically transmitting the state with the help of shared entanglement and limited classical communication. We show that it is poss…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062431] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that path superposition can activate perfect quantum teleportation using separable states, challenging the conventional link between entanglement and teleportation.
motivation: Quantum teleportation typically requires entanglement; this work explores whether separable states can achieve perfect teleportation via path superposition, which could have implications for quantum communication.
method: The authors propose a protocol where the sender and receiver use path superposition (coherent control over multiple paths) to teleport an unknown quantum state, analyzing the fidelity and separability conditions.
result: They demonstrate that with path superposition, separable states can achieve perfect teleportation fidelity, contrary to the usual requirement of entanglement.
conclusion: Path superposition provides a new resource for quantum teleportation, expanding the understanding of quantum communication beyond entanglement.

title: Oh Molecule As A Quantum Probe To Jointly Estimate Electric And Magnetic Fields
authors: Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, And Matteo G. A. Paris
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, and Matteo G. A. Paris

The hydroxyl radical (the OH molecule) carries both electric and magnetic dipole moments and, as a diatomic molecule, admits a comparatively simple and accurate model. This makes it a natural quantum probe for the joint estimation of electric and magnetic fields. Here we study simultaneous estimatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062612] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The OH molecule is proposed as a quantum probe for simultaneous estimation of electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: To exploit the OH molecule's dual dipole moments for joint field sensing, leveraging its simple and accurate model.
method: The authors study simultaneous estimation using quantum parameter estimation theory, analyzing the achievable precision and trade-offs.
result: They derive bounds on the estimation precision and show that the OH molecule can serve as an effective multiparameter quantum probe.
conclusion: The OH molecule is a viable platform for joint electric and magnetic field sensing, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Reference-frame-independent Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Over Asymmetric Channels
authors: Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, And Kejin Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, and Kejin Wei

Reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (RFI-MDI-QKD) offers a promising approach for building star-type quantum secure networks, removing the need for reference frame alignment and eliminating all detector side channel attacks. While prior experiments con…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063715] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent QKD over asymmetric channels, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: To remove the need for reference frame alignment and eliminate detector side-channel attacks in QKD, enabling robust star-type quantum networks over asymmetric channels.
method: Implemented RFI-MDI-QKD protocol with asymmetric channel losses and misalignment, using polarization encoding and decoy-state method.
result: Achieved secure key rates over asymmetric channels with significant misalignment, demonstrating feasibility for real-world networks.
conclusion: RFI-MDI-QKD is practical for asymmetric channel conditions, paving the way for scalable quantum secure networks.

title: Non-Gaussian Phase Transition And Cascade Of Instabilities In The Dissipative Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, And Thomas Barthel
abstract:
Author(s): Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, and Thomas Barthel

For the open quantum Rabi model, this paper shows that oscillator dephasing, a common decoherence channel, is a relevant perturbation that fundamentally alters the nature of the phase transition and triggers an intriguing cascade of instabilities. The authors also establish a new bridge between driven-dissipative systems and non-Hermitian quantum mechanics, where the Green’s-function dynamics are generated by simple non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061703] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that oscillator dephasing fundamentally alters the phase transition in the dissipative quantum Rabi model, leading to a cascade of instabilities, and establishes a bridge to non-Hermitian quantum mechanics.
motivation: Understanding the effect of common decoherence channels on phase transitions in driven-dissipative systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the open quantum Rabi model with oscillator dephasing using Green's function dynamics and map it to non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.
result: They find that dephasing is a relevant perturbation that changes the nature of the phase transition and triggers a cascade of instabilities.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and the role of dissipation in quantum phase transitions.

title: Superradiant Interactions For Relic Detection With Entangled Nuclear Spins
authors: Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, And Savas Dimopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, and Savas Dimopoulos

We recently showed that macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles prepared in coherent spin states can dramatically enhance the interaction rates of weakly interacting cosmic relics, such as dark matter and the cosmic neutrino background, through collective quantum effects analogous to Dicke superradiance,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063714] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles in coherent spin states to enhance detection of weakly interacting cosmic relics via superradiant collective effects.
motivation: Detecting dark matter and cosmic neutrino background is extremely challenging due to weak interaction cross-sections; collective quantum effects can amplify signals.
method: The authors analyze superradiant interactions in entangled nuclear spin ensembles, leveraging Dicke superradiance to enhance interaction rates with cosmic relics.
result: They show that macroscopic spin ensembles can dramatically increase detection rates, making previously inaccessible relic signals observable.
conclusion: This approach offers a new pathway for relic detection using quantum-enhanced sensing with nuclear spins, bridging quantum optics and particle physics.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermometry Via An Ensemble Of Initially Correlated Qubits
authors: Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, And Stefano Gherardini
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, and Stefano Gherardini

We investigate a nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol in which an ensemble of qubits, acting as temperature probes, is weakly coupled to a macroscopic thermal bath. The temperature of the bath, the parameter of interest, is encoded in the dissipator of a Markovian thermalization process. For …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062208] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol using an ensemble of initially correlated qubits to measure bath temperature.
motivation: Improving temperature estimation at the quantum scale by leveraging initial correlations among probe qubits.
method: Weakly couples an ensemble of qubits to a Markovian thermal bath, encoding temperature in the dissipator, and analyzes the quantum Fisher information.
result: Initial correlations can enhance the precision of temperature estimation beyond the standard limit.
conclusion: Correlated probes offer a resource for quantum thermometry in nonequilibrium settings.

title: Non-Markovianity-based Ultrasensitive Parameter Estimation
authors: Olli Siltanen
abstract:
Author(s): Olli Siltanen

Accurate parameter estimation is a central task in quantum metrology and sensing, where quantum resources can provide precision beyond classical limits. In realistic settings, however, system-environment interactions lead to decoherence, reducing these strategies to their classical counterparts. Noi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062427] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovianity can enhance parameter estimation precision beyond the standard quantum limit, using a qubit coupled to a structured environment.
motivation: Standard quantum metrology suffers from decoherence due to Markovian noise, limiting precision. Non-Markovian environments may offer a resource to overcome this.
method: The authors model a qubit sensor coupled to a structured environment with memory effects, derive the quantum Fisher information, and compare estimation precision under Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Non-Markovianity leads to a significant enhancement in the estimation precision, achieving scaling beyond the standard quantum limit in certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity can be harnessed as a resource for ultrasensitive parameter estimation, opening new avenues for quantum metrology in realistic noisy environments.

title: Scaling Bound Entanglement Through Local Extensions
authors: Robin Krebs And Mariami Gachechiladze
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Krebs and Mariami Gachechiladze

Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information science, yet its structure in high dimensions remains notoriously difficult to characterize. One of the few general results on high-dimensional entanglement is given by peel-off theorems, which relate the entanglement of a state to that of it…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062428] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a scaling law for bound entanglement in high-dimensional systems using local extensions.
motivation: Understanding the structure of high-dimensional entanglement is crucial for quantum information processing, but bound entanglement remains poorly characterized.
method: The authors develop a peel-off theorem that relates the entanglement of a state to that of its local extensions, and apply it to construct families of bound entangled states with increasing dimension.
result: They show that bound entanglement can be scaled up systematically, providing new examples of bound entangled states and revealing a hierarchical structure.
conclusion: The results advance the theory of entanglement in high dimensions and may have implications for quantum cryptography and resource theories.

title: Double-bracket Master Equations: Phase-space Representation And Classical Limit
authors: Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, and Adolfo del Campo

We systematically investigate master equations involving double-bracket dissipators in the classical limit. Dissipators defined by double commutators arise naturally in dephasing dynamics, while those defined by double anticommutators are typically associated with noisy Hamiltonians. The classical l…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062610] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates double-bracket master equations in the classical limit, connecting quantum dephasing and noisy Hamiltonians to classical stochastic processes.
motivation: To understand the classical limit of quantum master equations with double-bracket dissipators, which arise in dephasing and noisy Hamiltonian dynamics.
method: The authors use phase-space representations (e.g., Wigner function) and derive classical Fokker-Planck equations from the quantum master equations in the semiclassical limit.
result: They show that double-bracket dissipators lead to classical diffusion and drift terms, with explicit forms for the classical limit of dephasing and noisy Hamiltonian dynamics.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum and classical thermodynamics by providing a clear classical analogue of double-bracket dissipators, relevant for understanding decoherence and thermalization.

title: Equilibration And The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis As Limits To Observing Macroscopic Quantum Superpositions
authors: Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Macroscopic quantum superpositions are widely believed to be unobservable because large systems cannot be perfectly isolated from their environments. Here, we show that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as analyzed through the eigenstate thermaliz…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062207] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as described by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, can prevent the observation of macroscopic quantum superpositions.
motivation: To understand whether macroscopic quantum superpositions are fundamentally unobservable due to internal dynamics rather than environmental decoherence.
method: Analyzes the unitary evolution of many-body systems using the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) to show that initial superpositions of macroscopically distinct states rapidly equilibrate to a thermal state, suppressing interference.
result: The equilibration time scales polynomially with system size, and the superposition becomes effectively unobservable after a short time, even without any coupling to an external environment.
conclusion: Intrinsic many-body dynamics impose a fundamental limit on the observability of macroscopic quantum superpositions, independent of environmental decoherence.

title: Entanglement With A Mode Observable Via A Tunable Interaction With A Qubit
authors: Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, And Katarzyna Roszak
abstract:
Author(s): Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, and Katarzyna Roszak

We study the possibility of detection of “spin-boson” entanglement by qubit-only measurements. Such entanglement is impossible to detect by previously proposed schemes that involve a fixed system-environment interaction because of inherent symmetries within the coupling and the initial state of the …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062422] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a method to detect spin-boson entanglement using only qubit measurements via a tunable interaction.
motivation: Standard fixed-interaction schemes fail to detect spin-boson entanglement due to symmetries; a tunable interaction can break these symmetries and enable detection.
method: The authors analyze a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode via a tunable interaction, deriving conditions under which qubit-only measurements can reveal entanglement.
result: They show that by modulating the interaction, the qubit's reduced state can encode information about the entanglement, allowing detection without accessing the bosonic mode.
conclusion: Tunable interactions provide a practical route to witness hybrid entanglement in systems like circuit QED or spin-ensemble setups.

title: Tunable Spin-spin Coupling Mediated By Phonons In One-dimensional Systems And Its Application To Color Centers In Hexagonal Boron Nitride Ribbons
authors: Jotaro J. Nakane And Ai Yamakage
abstract:
Author(s): Jotaro J. Nakane and Ai Yamakage

We show that flexural phonons mediate tunable spin-spin interactions beyond nearest neighbors in one-dimensional systems. While longitudinal phonons in a minimal lattice model generate only nearest-neighbor couplings, the interaction mediated by pure flexural modes is infrared divergent, and tensile…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214433] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that flexural phonons in one-dimensional systems mediate tunable long-range spin-spin interactions, with application to color centers in hexagonal boron nitride ribbons.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin-spin interactions mediated by phonons is crucial for quantum information processing in solid-state platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a one-dimensional lattice model with spin-phonon coupling, considering both longitudinal and flexural phonon modes, and derive effective spin-spin interactions.
result: Flexural phonons induce infrared-divergent, long-range interactions that can be tuned by tensile strain, while longitudinal phonons give only nearest-neighbor couplings.
conclusion: The tunable interactions mediated by flexural phonons can be exploited for quantum simulation and information processing using color centers in hexagonal boron nitride ribbons.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but existing methods are often inefficient for topologically ordered systems like the toric code.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, enabling efficient Gibbs sampling using classical Monte Carlo methods.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the duality provides a rigorous bound on the mixing time of the quantum Gibbs sampler.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach to Gibbs state preparation for topologically ordered systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation.

title: Extending The Dynamic Range In Quantum Frequency Estimation With Sequential Weak Measurements
authors: Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, And Tuvia Gefen
abstract:
Author(s): Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, and Tuvia Gefen

A sequential weak measurement protocol is developed for Bayesian quantum frequency estimation with coherent spin states in which weakly entangled ancilla qubits track the sensing qubits during free evolution to suppress phase slip errors and extend the dynamic range. The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound asymptotically across a large frequency bandwidth.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022046] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A sequential weak measurement protocol for quantum frequency estimation that uses weakly entangled ancilla qubits to suppress phase slip errors and extend dynamic range, achieving Heisenberg scaling and saturating the Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Quantum frequency estimation is limited by phase slip errors that reduce dynamic range; existing methods trade off precision for range. The authors aim to overcome this using weak measurements and entanglement.
method: The protocol employs sequential weak measurements on coherent spin states, with weakly entangled ancilla qubits tracking the sensing qubits during free evolution. Bayesian inference is used to estimate frequency from measurement outcomes.
result: The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and asymptotically saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound across a large frequency bandwidth, significantly extending the dynamic range compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Sequential weak measurements with ancilla entanglement provide a practical route to high-precision, wide-dynamic-range quantum frequency estimation, relevant for quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on the information that can be extracted from neural activity via MEG, constrained by metabolic energy and quantum sensing bounds.
method: Applies the energy resolution limit from quantum metrology and the metabolic power available to neural currents to compute an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets a fundamental upper bound on the information capacity of MEG, linking quantum sensing limits to biological energy constraints.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic and quantum-information bound on MEG performance, highlighting the interplay between energy dissipation and information extraction in biological systems.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień
