conclusion: The proposed transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable candidate for practical fault-tolerant quantum simulation, reducing resource requirements by orders of magnitude.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory to derive bounds on the variance of the loss function and its dependence on circuit depth, noise rate, and expressivity.
result: They find that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to a concentration of the loss function that is less severe than in the noiseless case, and provide explicit estimates for the variance.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit expressivity, potentially improving the trainability of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to study string breaking in quantum spin models, comparing adiabatic and diabatic regimes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including non-adiabatic effects and entanglement generation.
conclusion: String breaking dynamics provide a new probe of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and can be observed in current quantum simulators.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise models can significantly enhance the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, aiding in algorithm development and error mitigation.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration and logical rotation gates.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy estimates on current hardware.
method: Implements noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion processor to compute molecular energies.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to near-term quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for reliable quantum advantage in molecular science.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, quantum information, and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to relate them. This review aims to unify these approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical techniques such as hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: A unified perspective on non-Markovian dynamics helps bridge gaps between subfields and facilitates progress in quantum technologies.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and circuit depth.
motivation: Qudits offer a more efficient representation for certain quantum gates and algorithms, potentially reducing resource requirements compared to qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can simplify multiqubit gates like Toffoli and enable more efficient quantum algorithm realizations, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, though challenges in control and error correction remain; further development could lead to practical advantages.

title: Universal Composite Phase Gates With Tunable Target Phase
authors: Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, And Andon A. Rangelov
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, and Andon A. Rangelov

We present a systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with a continuously tunable target phase. Using a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of the single-pulse propagator, we design gates from an even number of nominal [MATH] pulses and derive analytic phase families by cance…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with continuously tunable target phase using Cayley-Klein parametrization.
motivation: Composite pulses are essential for robust quantum control, but existing methods often fix the target phase; this work aims to provide tunability for greater flexibility in quantum gates.
method: The authors use a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of single-pulse propagators and design gates from an even number of nominal π pulses, deriving analytic phase families by canceling error terms.
result: They demonstrate universal composite phase gates that can achieve any target phase continuously, with robustness against pulse area errors.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a versatile tool for quantum control, enabling precise phase gates that are useful in quantum information processing.

title: Error Convergence Of Quantum Linear System Solvers
authors: Matias Ginzburg And Ugo Marzolino
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Ginzburg and Ugo Marzolino

The Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm remains a paradigmatic quantum routine for solving linear systems and a widely used benchmark in theoretical and experimental studies. Several circuit-level variants have been proposed to simplify its implementation, including constructions in which the cloc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062436] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the error convergence of quantum linear system solvers, focusing on the HHL algorithm and its variants.
motivation: Understanding the error behavior of quantum linear system solvers is crucial for practical implementation and benchmarking.
method: The authors study the convergence of errors in HHL-type algorithms, considering different clock constructions and noise models.
result: They derive bounds on the error as a function of the number of qubits and circuit depth, showing trade-offs between accuracy and resource requirements.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the practical limitations of quantum linear system solvers, but does not introduce new information-theoretic or thermodynamic results.

title: Global Versus Local Discrimination Of Locally Implementable Multipartite Unitaries
authors: Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, and Debashis Saha

We study single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) and global operations. As unitary discrimination depends on both the choice of probing states and the measurements on the evolved states, we classify LOCC…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062209] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under LOCC and global operations, classifying LOCC strategies.
motivation: Understanding the power and limitations of LOCC in discriminating quantum operations is fundamental to quantum information processing.
method: The authors classify LOCC strategies and compare their performance to global operations for distinguishing locally implementable unitaries.
result: They provide a classification of LOCC strategies and show that global operations can outperform LOCC in certain cases.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of quantum operation discrimination, highlighting the gap between local and global capabilities.

title: Globalized Critical Quantum Metrology In The Dynamics Of The Quantum Rabi Model By An Auxiliary Nonlinear Term
authors: Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, and Zu-Jian Ying

The quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model for light-matter interactions; the finite-component quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM has established a paradigmatic application for critical quantum metrology (CQM). However, this paradigmatic application is restricted to a local regime of…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062423] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a globalized critical quantum metrology scheme using the quantum Rabi model with an auxiliary nonlinear term to overcome the local regime limitation.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology in the quantum Rabi model is limited to a local regime; the authors aim to extend it to a global regime by introducing a nonlinear term.
method: They analyze the dynamics of the quantum Rabi model with an added nonlinear term, studying the quantum phase transition and its impact on metrological sensitivity.
result: The auxiliary nonlinear term enables globalized critical quantum metrology, enhancing sensitivity beyond the local regime.
conclusion: The proposed scheme broadens the applicability of critical quantum metrology in light-matter interaction systems.

title: Quantum Complexity And Localization In Random And Time-periodic Unitary Circuits
authors: Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, And Pingal Pratyush Nath
abstract:
Author(s): Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, and Pingal Pratyush Nath

We study the growth and saturation of complexity in Krylov basis in random quantum circuits. In Haar-random unitary evolution, we show that, for large system sizes, this notion of complexity grows linearly before saturating at a late-time value of [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hilbert space dimension, at …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214312] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Krylov complexity growth in random and time-periodic unitary circuits, finding linear growth and saturation to a maximal value.
motivation: Understanding complexity growth in quantum circuits is important for characterizing quantum chaos and the limits of quantum computation.
method: The authors analyze Krylov complexity in Haar-random unitary circuits and Floquet systems using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They show that Krylov complexity grows linearly with time and saturates at a value proportional to the Hilbert space dimension, with the saturation time scaling logarithmically in system size.
conclusion: Krylov complexity provides a useful measure of quantum complexity in random circuits, with behavior reminiscent of operator growth in chaotic systems.

title: Lieb-Robinson Causality And non-Fermi Liquids
authors: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Aditya Hebbar, And Sean A. Hartnoll
abstract:
Author(s): Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Aditya Hebbar, and Sean A. Hartnoll

Here, the authors show that the Lieb-Robinson causality bound, a fundamental result in quantum lattice physics, implies a first-principles and model-independent bound on certain non-Fermi liquid coupling constants. The work demonstrates that methods from the modern S-matrix bootstrap in high-energy physics — in particular, analyticity constraints in both the complex energy and momentum planes — can be adapted to condensed matter lattice models.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245125] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Lieb-Robinson causality bounds to derive model-independent constraints on non-Fermi liquid coupling constants.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits on non-Fermi liquid behavior from causality principles.
method: Adapts S-matrix bootstrap analyticity constraints to condensed matter lattice models, combining complex energy and momentum plane methods.
result: Derives first-principles bounds on certain non-Fermi liquid coupling constants.
conclusion: Lieb-Robinson bounds provide a powerful tool for constraining strongly correlated systems beyond traditional methods.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improve accuracy and efficiency of VQE for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices.
method: Constructs an ansatz based on an approximate multiqubit target state and quantum information measures.
result: Demonstrates improved ground-state energy estimates for atomic systems compared to heuristic ansätze.
conclusion: The proposed ansatz is effective for atomic systems but may not generalize broadly.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Q-FLARE, an iterative method to learn quantum feature maps with reduced circuit depth and fewer qubits.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources; quantum feature maps in QML often require deep circuits that are not feasible on near-term devices.
method: Proposes an analytic iterative reconstruction algorithm that learns a feature map by alternating between classical optimization and quantum circuit updates, reducing resource overhead.
result: Demonstrates that the learned feature maps achieve comparable or better classification accuracy with significantly fewer gates and qubits than standard approaches.
conclusion: Q-FLARE enables more efficient quantum feature maps, making QML more practical for near-term quantum hardware.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters for scalable generation of optical non-Gaussian quantum states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; this work aims to optimize the process.
method: The authors propose new control parameters that systematically optimize the generation of non-Gaussian states in optical systems.
result: The new parameters increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.
conclusion: This breakthrough enables scalable and efficient generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for characterizing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate and constant-depth encoding circuits, enabling fault-tolerant magic state distillation.
result: Tricycle codes achieve high thresholds and low overhead for magic state generation, outperforming existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path to reduce the cost of magic states in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical simulation method for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding and simulating quantum expectation landscapes is important for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly. The authors aim to reduce this cost by focusing on small patches.
method: The method uses a classical surrogate model trained on a limited number of quantum measurements to predict expectation values for nearby points in the landscape, leveraging locality and smoothness.
result: The approach achieves efficient classical simulation of patches with provable guarantees, reducing the quantum resource requirements for exploring the landscape.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for hybrid quantum-classical optimization, though it is more about classical simulation than core quantum information theory.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting strong and weak symmetries to optimize stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become inefficient for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. Symmetries can reduce the effective Hilbert space dimension.
method: The authors develop algorithms that leverage strong (exact) and weak (approximate) symmetries to decompose multiqubit unitaries into stabilizer parts more efficiently, enabling simulation of larger circuits.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach renders optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits, significantly extending the reach of classical simulation.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of quantum circuits, particularly those dominated by Clifford gates, and can help bridge the gap between quantum and classical computation.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and Fisher information near critical points.
result: Demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing provides a promising route for high-precision metrology, but practical challenges remain.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation is introduced to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for products of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to merge or cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in T-count for certain quantum circuits, demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: The work provides a new algebraic tool for T-count optimization, contributing to resource-efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, allowing classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols without tracking all intermediate errors.
result: The method significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating magic state preparation, enabling the study of larger codes and higher-distance protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, which is important for resource estimation and optimization in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without needing extra ancilla blocks, preserving the code's performance characteristics.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations on low-overhead quantum codes.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectra.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of quantum systems is important but worst-case complexity is high; the paper aims to provide a practical quantum algorithm for eigenvalue clustering.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to identify clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities, leveraging quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral structures, enabling analysis of eigenvalue multiplicities.
conclusion: The work presents a quantum algorithm for spectral analysis that is useful for quantum information tasks but is more algorithmic than information-theoretic.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, including gates, measurements, and high-rate code constructions.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana qubits requires tailored error correction and logical operations due to fermionic statistics.
method: The authors generalize qubit-based fault-tolerant techniques to fermionic systems, designing transversal gates, measurement schemes, and high-rate quantum codes.
result: They demonstrate that fault-tolerant operations are possible in Majorana codes with improved thresholds and resource overhead.
conclusion: Majorana-based quantum codes can support universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with practical advantages.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements in various fields exceed them, prompting a need to understand why and how to design materials that exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, homogeneity, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common patterns of assumption violations and shows that materials can be designed to deliberately break these assumptions, leading to properties beyond classical limits.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations of thermodynamics but rather indicate that the bounds' assumptions are not met; this insight can guide the development of novel materials with extreme properties.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves force sensitivity below the standard quantum limit by measuring a levitated nanoparticle's motion.
motivation: To detect extremely weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter interactions, by surpassing the zero-point fluctuation limit.
method: Optical levitation and interferometric measurement of a nanoparticle's motion, with feedback cooling to reduce thermal noise.
result: Demonstrated force sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations, enabling detection of forces at the attonewton scale.
conclusion: The technique opens new possibilities for fundamental physics searches and ultra-sensitive force detection.

title: Exceptional Points Of Arbitrary High Orders Induced By non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, And Alexander A. Zyablovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, and Alexander A. Zyablovsky

Exceptional points are singularities in the spectrum of non-Hermitian systems in which several eigenvectors are linearly dependent and their eigenvalues are equal to each other. Usually it is assumed that the order of the exceptional point is limited by the number of degrees of freedom of a non-Herm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062212] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovian dynamics can induce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order in open quantum systems, overcoming the usual limitation by the number of degrees of freedom.
motivation: Exceptional points are typically limited in order by the system's degrees of freedom; the authors aim to demonstrate that non-Markovian effects can bypass this restriction.
method: They analyze a model of a quantum system coupled to a structured environment with memory, using non-Markovian master equations to study the spectral properties.
result: They find that non-Markovian dynamics can produce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order, even in systems with few degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity provides a new mechanism for generating high-order exceptional points, with potential applications in sensing and control.

title: Maximum Heralding Probabilities Of Nonclassical-state Generation From A Two-mode Gaussian State Via Photon-counting Measurements
authors: Jaromír Fiurášek
abstract:
Author(s): Jaromír Fiurášek

Highly nonclassical states of light—such as the approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, states exhibiting cubic nonlinear squeezing, or catlike states—can be generated from experimentally accessible Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements on selected modes, conditioned on specific out…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063716] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum heralding probabilities for generating nonclassical states from two-mode Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements.
motivation: Nonclassical states like GKP states are important for quantum information processing, but their generation via heralding is probabilistic; maximizing success probability is crucial.
method: The author formulates an optimization problem over Gaussian states and measurement patterns to maximize the heralding probability for a target nonclassical state, using semidefinite programming and analytical bounds.
result: Explicit upper bounds on heralding probabilities are derived for various target states, showing fundamental limits and trade-offs between state quality and success rate.
conclusion: The results provide guidelines for experimental design and highlight the inherent probabilistic nature of heralded nonclassical state generation.

title: Anomalous Thermodynamics Of Lattice Bose Gases In Optical Cavities
authors: Liang He And Su Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Liang He and Su Yi

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of lattice Bose gases in optical cavities in the Mott-insulator limit. We find that the system assumes anomalous thermodynamic behavior that can be traced back to the breaking of fundamental additivity by its infinite-long-range interaction. Specifically, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063313] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Lattice Bose gases in optical cavities exhibit anomalous thermodynamics due to infinite-range interactions breaking additivity.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions in cavity QED systems affect thermodynamic properties beyond standard statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical and numerical study of the Mott-insulator limit of the Bose-Hubbard model with cavity-mediated infinite-range interactions.
result: The system shows non-additive thermodynamics, with phase transitions and critical behavior modified by the cavity field.
conclusion: Infinite-range interactions lead to qualitatively new thermodynamic phenomena, relevant for quantum simulators and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: The paper derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, extending the concept beyond the standard Heisenberg-Robertson relation.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for minimum uncertainty and squeezed states using a stronger sum uncertainty relation, which may offer new insights into quantum correlations.
method: The authors use the sum uncertainty relation proposed by Maccone and Pati to derive conditions for minimum uncertainty states and apply them to single-mode and two-mode systems, identifying squeezed states.
result: They show that the sum uncertainty relation yields a broader class of minimum uncertainty states, including squeezed states, and discuss their properties.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation provides a more general characterization of minimum uncertainty and squeezed states, potentially useful for quantum information applications.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes fault-tolerant cat state preparation for quantum error correction, focusing on reducing resource overhead at large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them with high fidelity at large distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale.
method: The authors propose a systematic optimization framework that combines circuit synthesis and error correction code constraints to minimize the number of gates and ancilla qubits needed for cat state preparation.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in gate count and qubit overhead compared to standard methods, enabling preparation of cat states at fault distances up to 11 with practical resources.
conclusion: The optimized protocols make large-distance cat state preparation feasible, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Dressed Bound States And non-Markovian Dynamics With A Whispering-gallery-mode Microcavity Coupled To A Two-level Atom And A Semi-infinite Photonic Waveguide
authors: J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We investigate dressed bound states in an open cavity with a whispering-gallery-mode microring coupled to a two-level atom and a waveguide with a mirror at the right end. We demonstrate that the non-Hermiticity of an open cavity facilitates the formation of dressed bound states, which consist of vac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063713] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dressed bound states and non-Markovian dynamics in an open cavity system coupled to a waveguide, focusing on the role of non-Hermiticity in bound state formation.
motivation: Understanding bound states in open quantum systems is important for controlling dissipation and coherence, which has implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors model a whispering-gallery-mode microcavity coupled to a two-level atom and a semi-infinite waveguide with a mirror, using analytical and numerical methods to solve for dressed bound states and dynamics.
result: They find that non-Hermiticity from the open cavity enables the formation of dressed bound states, which suppress spontaneous emission and lead to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling quantum dynamics in open systems, potentially useful for quantum memory or single-photon sources.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades under environmental interaction.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but its dependence on phase-space scales is not fully characterized.
method: The authors use phase-space methods (e.g., Wigner function) to quantify decoherence for compass states and extend the analysis to general quantum states, examining scaling behavior.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale, with larger scales more robust, and provide a unified framework for predicting decoherence dynamics.
conclusion: The work offers insights into decoherence mitigation by identifying scale-dependent robustness, but does not introduce new information-theoretic or thermodynamic results.

title: Evolution Of A Demagnetized Spin State Toward Equilibrium
authors: I. A. Yastremsky And B. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Yastremsky and B. A. Ivanov

The temporal evolution of the nonequilibrium nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state is analyzed within the general phenomenological spin-dynamics theory proposed by Baryakhtar, which employs the concepts of both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation. We demonstrate that strong…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224422] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the temporal evolution of a demagnetized ferromagnetic state toward equilibrium using a phenomenological spin-dynamics theory with local and nonlocal relaxation.
motivation: Understanding the relaxation dynamics of nonequilibrium spin states is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in spintronics.
method: The authors employ Baryakhtar's phenomenological spin-dynamics theory, which includes both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation mechanisms.
result: They demonstrate that strong nonlocal relaxation can lead to specific evolution patterns of the spin state toward equilibrium.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of exchange relaxation in the equilibration of ferromagnetic spin systems.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
authors: Noa Feldman And Moshe Goldstein
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universal corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor network methods.
motivation: Understanding the universal corner term in entanglement entropy provides insight into quantum field theories and critical phenomena.
method: The authors use tensor network techniques, specifically matrix product states and projected entangled pair states, to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with sharp corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution emerges naturally from lattice discretization and matches field theory predictions.
conclusion: Tensor networks are a powerful tool for extracting universal entanglement features in lattice models.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-averaged displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, focusing on scaling laws for anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding single-particle tracking dynamics is important for characterizing transport in complex systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function applicable to both normal and anomalous diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing single-particle tracking data, but has no direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under two types of Poissonian resetting, analyzing the relaxation to a non-equilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand the effect of resetting on underdamped dynamics, which is relevant for stochastic thermodynamics and control of small systems.
method: Analytical and numerical solutions of the underdamped Langevin equation with resetting events that either reset both position and velocity or only position with velocity drawn from Maxwell distribution.
result: The system reaches a non-equilibrium steady state; the relaxation time and steady-state properties depend on the resetting procedure and damping.
conclusion: Resetting protocols can be used to engineer steady states in underdamped systems, with potential applications in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion induce directed motion and negative mobility in overdamped stochastic systems.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries can generate directed motion and negative mobility in stochastic systems, which is relevant to transport in confined geometries.
method: Analytical and numerical study of overdamped Langevin dynamics with anisotropic diffusion tensor and hard reflecting boundaries, using no-flux conditions and trajectory analysis.
result: Boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion generically produces directed motion and can lead to negative mobility, where the system moves opposite to an applied force.
conclusion: The findings reveal a generic mechanism for directed transport in confined stochastic systems, with implications for understanding transport in biological and nanoscale systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: Understanding anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic approach to compute exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: Exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, showing anomalous behavior.
conclusion: The hydrodynamic method successfully captures the anomalous fluctuations in these stochastic systems.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, enabling the study of quantum phase transitions in the resulting spin systems.
method: The authors use trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to define ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then analyze the quantum phase transition when a transverse field is added.
result: They characterize the quantum phase transition for each of the 256 elementary cellular automata rules, showing how the CA rule determines the nature of the transition.
conclusion: Cellular automata provide a systematic way to generate classical spin models with tunable quantum phase transitions, linking computational and physical systems.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting entanglement in high-energy photons where standard polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for the two-photon state to be a Bell state, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for quantum information processing with high-energy photons, but the connection to the user's core interests in quantum information theory is indirect.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, which have no equilibrium counterpart.
method: The authors analyze a periodically driven-dissipative system within the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation, focusing on the Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: They identify topological features and nonreciprocal transport in the open Floquet chain.
conclusion: The work extends topological concepts to open driven systems, but is not directly aligned with core information thermodynamics interests.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness measures for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve for H2 and other dimers.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, but the work is more of an application of existing measures rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information theory.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: Employs Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables and operator growth in Floquet systems, leveraging spectral representations.
result: FNOs accurately predict dynamics beyond training time windows and generalize to different driving parameters, demonstrating faithful modeling of Floquet Hamiltonians.
conclusion: FNOs provide an efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, enabling extrapolation and reduced computational cost.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to distinguish topologically protected Majorana modes from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their properties.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to evaluate Majorana bound states in realistic devices, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational algorithm that identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes in a multimode squeezed light source, enabling compression of the processor's mode count.
result: The approach reduces the required hardware footprint from quadratic to near-constant scaling while maintaining processing fidelity.
conclusion: Variational supermode selection offers a practical path to scalable multimode photonic quantum information processing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective actions for a wide class of systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications beyond chemistry.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory simulations.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions, such as photodoping and transient order, and discusses metastable superconducting and magnetic states.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Observation Of Five Distinct Localization Phases In A 1d Floquet System
authors: Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, And Jingyun Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, and Jingyun Fan

Extended, localized, and critical states form the three elementary classes of eigenstates underlying Anderson localization. While phases involving extended and localized states are widely studied, experimental realization of critical phases, particularly those where critical states coexist with othe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of five distinct localization phases in a 1D Floquet system, including critical phases.
motivation: To experimentally realize and characterize critical phases in disordered Floquet systems, which are less explored than extended and localized phases.
method: Using a photonic waveguide array with periodic driving and disorder to realize a 1D Floquet system, measuring wavefunction statistics and transport properties.
result: Five distinct phases are observed: extended, localized, and three types of critical phases with different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the richness of localization phenomena in Floquet systems and provides a platform for studying critical phases.

title: Two-point Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Gradients In The Frequency Domain
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, And Hong-Fu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, and Hong-Fu Wang

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a leading platform for combinatorial optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. A central challenge for QAOA and related variational algorithms is how to obtain efficient, provably reliable gradient estimators. We develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062425] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a frequency-domain analysis of QAOA gradients to improve optimization efficiency.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA suffer from inefficient gradient estimation; the authors aim to provide provably reliable gradient estimators.
method: They analyze QAOA gradients in the frequency domain, deriving expressions that relate gradient components to the problem Hamiltonian's spectrum.
result: The frequency-domain approach yields more efficient gradient computation and insights into the optimization landscape.
conclusion: The method offers a new perspective for optimizing QAOA, potentially improving performance on NISQ devices.

title: Optical Tautochrone And Squeezing Dynamics In Nonuniform Lattices
authors: Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, And Konstantinos G. Makris
abstract:
Author(s): Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, and Konstantinos G. Makris

We present exact analogies between the tautochrone problem of classical mechanics and the squeezed states of quantum optics to optical lattices. Both phenomena emerge in the same physical system, that of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings. Extension to two dimensions yields Lissajous-type tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper draws analogies between the classical tautochrone problem and quantum squeezing in nonuniform optical lattices, demonstrating exact solutions for waveguide arrays.
motivation: To explore connections between classical mechanics and quantum optics in the context of optical lattices with nonuniform couplings.
method: The authors derive exact analytical solutions for waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings, showing that both tautochrone and squeezing dynamics emerge from the same system.
result: They find that nonuniform lattices can exhibit both tautochrone (isochronous) oscillations and squeezing dynamics, and extend the analysis to two dimensions yielding Lissajous-type trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework linking classical and quantum phenomena in optical lattices, with potential applications in quantum simulation and control.

title: Exotic Critical States As Fractional Fermi Seas In The One-Dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, And Manuele Landini
abstract:
Author(s): Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, and Manuele Landini

Critical quantum field theories occupy a central position in modern theoretical physics for their inherent universality stemming from long-range correlations. As an example, the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) describes a wealth of one-dimensional quantum systems at low temperatures. Its behavior is…

tldr: This paper studies exotic critical states in a one-dimensional Bose gas, interpreting them as fractional Fermi seas, which is a topic in quantum many-body physics and ultracold atoms.
motivation: To understand the nature of exotic critical states in one-dimensional Bose gases beyond the standard Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid description.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with experimental realization in a Bose gas, using techniques from quantum field theory and ultracold atom experiments.
result: Identifies fractional Fermi sea states as a new class of critical states in one-dimensional Bose gases.
conclusion: These exotic critical states extend the known universality classes of one-dimensional quantum systems and may have implications for quantum simulation.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing.
