tldr: This paper studies coherent spin and valley dynamics in a 2D material heterostructure using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect, with subpicosecond control.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information storage and processing in spin-and-valley-tronic devices.
method: Time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy and theoretical modeling of the magnetic proximity effect in a heterostructure.
result: Demonstrated subpicosecond coherent control of spin and valley pseudospin via the anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
conclusion: The approach enables ultrafast coherent manipulation of spin and valley degrees of freedom, relevant for quantum information applications.

title: Photodetection Of Squeezed Light: A Whittaker-Shannon Analysis
authors: Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, And J. E. Sipe
abstract:
Author(s): Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, and J. E. Sipe

The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition provides a temporally localized description of squeezed light, making it applicable in the continuous-wave limit and leading to a definition of squeezing strength based on the number of photon pairs at a time. We show examples of its usefulness by calculating quad…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063719] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to analyze squeezed light in the continuous-wave limit, focusing on photodetection and squeezing strength.
motivation: To provide a temporally localized description of squeezed light that is applicable in the continuous-wave limit, improving the analysis of photodetection.
method: Uses the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to define a squeezing strength based on photon pair number and calculates quadrature variances.
result: Demonstrates the usefulness of the decomposition for calculating quadrature variances and characterizing squeezed light.
conclusion: The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition offers a valuable tool for describing squeezed light in continuous-wave photodetection scenarios.

title: Biorthogonal Scattering And Generalized Unitarity In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, And Hee Chul Park
abstract:
Author(s): Jung-Wan Ryu, Henning Schomerus, and Hee Chul Park

We investigate the two-port scattering process in non-Hermitian dimer models via quantum measurements using external leads. We focus on two exemplary dimer models that preserve parity-time symmetry via spatial gain-loss balance and exhibit nonreciprocity due to directional hopping. The scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062213] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models with parity-time symmetry and nonreciprocity, focusing on biorthogonal scattering and generalized unitarity.
motivation: To understand scattering processes in non-Hermitian systems, which are relevant for open quantum systems and photonics, but not directly tied to the user's core interests.
method: The authors analyze two-port scattering in non-Hermitian dimer models using external leads, employing biorthogonal quantum mechanics and scattering matrix formalism.
result: They derive generalized unitarity relations and characterize scattering properties such as transmission and reflection in the presence of gain and loss.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for scattering in non-Hermitian systems but does not advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Distillation Of Topological Boundary States Via non-Hermitian Masking
authors: Juan Kang, Chaohua Wu, Keran Li, Shuo Liu, Qinglong Zhang, And Gang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Juan Kang, Chaohua Wu, Keran Li, Shuo Liu, Qinglong Zhang, and Gang Chen

Topological boundary states are a hallmark of topological phases, yet their direct detection remains challenging when they hybridize with bulk states or fail to form isolated in-gap modes. Here, we introduce a dynamical approach for directly distilling boundary-localized states in topological lattic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063514] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A dynamical method to distill topological boundary states using non-Hermitian masking in photonic lattices.
motivation: Topological boundary states are often obscured by hybridization with bulk states; direct detection is challenging.
method: Introduces a non-Hermitian masking technique that dynamically amplifies boundary-localized states while suppressing bulk contributions.
result: Demonstrates successful distillation of topological boundary states in a photonic lattice, enabling clear detection.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian masking provides a practical tool for probing topological boundary states in experiments.

title: Out-of-equilibrium Expansion Dynamics Of Dipolar Atoms In An Optical Lattice
authors: Barnali Chakrabarti, N. D. Chavda, Andrea Trombettoni, And Arnaldo Gammal
abstract:
Author(s): Barnali Chakrabarti, N. D. Chavda, Andrea Trombettoni, and Arnaldo Gammal

We investigate the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in finite one-dimensional lattice systems employing the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method, which enables a numerically exact treatment of full many-body correlations, quantum fragmentation, and long-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063312] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in 1D optical lattices using a numerically exact many-body method.
motivation: Understanding the expansion dynamics of dipolar quantum gases in optical lattices is important for probing out-of-equilibrium phenomena and many-body correlations.
method: The authors use the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method to simulate the full many-body dynamics of dipolar atoms in finite one-dimensional lattices.
result: They characterize the expansion dynamics, including the role of dipolar interactions and quantum statistics (bosons vs fermions), and observe fragmentation and correlation effects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium dynamics of dipolar systems but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Transport Scaling And Critical Tilt Effects In Disordered Two-dimensional Dirac Fermions
authors: Swadeepan Nanda And Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Swadeepan Nanda and Pavan Hosur

Two-dimensional (2D) Dirac fermions occur ubiquitously in condensed matter systems from topological phases to quantum critical points. Since the advent of topological semimetals, where the dispersion is often tilted around the band crossing where the Dirac fermion can appear, tilt has emerged as a k…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214203] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Studies transport scaling and critical tilt effects in disordered two-dimensional Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand how tilt in the Dirac dispersion affects transport properties in disordered systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using scaling theory and numerical simulations of disordered Dirac fermions with tilted cones.
result: Finds that tilt modifies the critical exponents and transport scaling behavior.
conclusion: Tilt is an important parameter in the transport physics of disordered Dirac materials.

title: Exact Mobility Edges And Hidden Self-duality In non-Hermitian Quasiperiodic Network Models
authors: San-Ren He, Jing Fan, Lin Li, Rui Wang, Dong-Hui Xu, And Zhen-Hua Wang
abstract:
Author(s): San-Ren He, Jing Fan, Lin Li, Rui Wang, Dong-Hui Xu, and Zhen-Hua Wang

The determination of the mobility edge (ME)—the critical energy threshold separating extended and localized quantum states—remains a central challenge in the study of Anderson transitions, particularly within complex non-Hermitian systems where conventional Hermitian techniques often fail. While the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224205] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact mobility edges in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic network models, focusing on Anderson transitions in complex systems.
motivation: Determining mobility edges in non-Hermitian systems is challenging and important for understanding localization phenomena.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic network model and uncover a hidden self-duality that allows exact calculation of mobility edges.
result: Exact mobility edges are derived, revealing the transition between extended and localized states in the non-Hermitian regime.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for mobility edges in non-Hermitian systems, advancing the theory of Anderson localization.

title: Time-dependent Fluctuating Local Field Approach For The Description Of Correlated Fermions Dynamics
authors: L. D. Silakov, Ya. S. Lyakhova, And A. N. Rubtsov
abstract:
Author(s): L. D. Silakov, Ya. S. Lyakhova, and A. N. Rubtsov

We formulate a time-dependent Fluctuating Local Field (TD-FLF) method for correlated fermion dynamics, extending the stationary FLF approach. The wave function is approximated as an ensemble of noninteracting states subject to a classical fluctuating field, with dynamics encoded in the field's time-…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235121] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A time-dependent extension of the fluctuating local field method for simulating correlated fermion dynamics.
motivation: To develop a computationally efficient method for describing the real-time dynamics of correlated fermionic systems beyond static approximations.
method: The wave function is approximated as an ensemble of noninteracting states subject to a classical fluctuating field, with dynamics encoded in the field's time-correlation function.
result: The method provides a way to capture dynamical correlations in fermionic systems using a stochastic mean-field approach.
conclusion: The TD-FLF method offers a practical tool for studying non-equilibrium dynamics of correlated fermions, though its accuracy depends on the field's fluctuation properties.

title: Single-particle Dynamical Signature Of Topology Induced By Single Mode Cavities In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: F. Pavan, G. Di Bello, G. de Filippis, And C. A. Perroni
abstract:
Author(s): F. Pavan, G. Di Bello, G. De Filippis, and C. A. Perroni

Witnessing and tracking topological phase transitions induced by interactions with the environment is a crucial challenge. Among the various experimental approaches to detect topological properties, the Mean Chiral Displacement (MCD) has emerged as a powerful bulk probe in one-dimensional chiral sys…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain induced by coupling to a single-mode cavity, using the mean chiral displacement as a probe.
motivation: To detect and track topological phase transitions induced by environmental interactions, which is a challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a single-particle SSH chain coupled to a single-mode cavity, computing the mean chiral displacement to characterize topological properties.
result: They find that the cavity can induce topological phase transitions and that the mean chiral displacement serves as a robust dynamical signature of topology.
conclusion: Cavity-induced topology can be probed via single-particle dynamics, offering a way to witness topological changes in open systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Equilibrium Josephson Effect Of Arbitrary Periodicity From Poor Man's Majorana Zero Modes
authors: Panagiotis Kotetes, Mercè Roig, And Brian M. Andersen

We show that the Josephson diode effect becomes possible when two coupled antiferromagnetic dimers of pointlike magnetic adatoms are deposited on top of a Rashba superconductor. The degree of nonreciprocity is substantial when the arising Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound states approach zero energy. In …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241403] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a nonreciprocal Josephson effect in a system of magnetic adatoms on a Rashba superconductor, mediated by Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states.
motivation: To demonstrate a Josephson diode effect with arbitrary periodicity using poor man's Majorana zero modes.
method: Theoretical analysis of two coupled antiferromagnetic dimers of magnetic adatoms on a Rashba superconductor, solving for the Andreev bound states and Josephson current.
result: Nonreciprocal Josephson effect with substantial diode efficiency when YSR states approach zero energy.
conclusion: The system provides a platform for a Josephson diode with tunable periodicity, relevant for superconducting spintronics.

title: Polaron-mediated Anisotropic Exchange In Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Johanna P. Carbone, Jakob Baumsteiger, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Johanna P. Carbone, Jakob Baumsteiger, and Cesare Franchini

Two-dimensional (2D) magnets offer a rich platform for exploring emergent spin phenomena due to their unique and diverse magnetic properties. Beyond intrinsic magnetism, external manipulation—such as defect engineering, molecular adsorption, or charge doping—offers powerful routes to control their m…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214428] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-mediated anisotropic exchange in 2D magnets, focusing on defect engineering and charge doping to control magnetic properties.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnetic interactions in 2D materials is important for spintronics and related applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and first-principles calculations to investigate how polarons mediate anisotropic exchange interactions.
result: They find that polaron formation can significantly modify the magnetic exchange coupling, leading to anisotropic behavior.
conclusion: Polaron-mediated exchange offers a route to tune magnetism in 2D materials via external doping or defects.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport at low driving frequencies.
motivation: To understand the effect of detuning the driving frequency on the Floquet chiral spin liquid and to characterize the transition from high-frequency effective static behavior to low-frequency anomalous transport.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and effective Hamiltonian approaches to analyze the driven spin system, focusing on the Floquet formalism and the emergence of chiral spin liquid phases.
result: They find that at low frequencies, the system realizes 'Swap' models with anomalous chiral spin liquid phases exhibiting one-way spin transport, distinct from the high-frequency effective static chiral spin liquid.
conclusion: The work provides insights into Floquet engineering of topological phases and the role of driving frequency in stabilizing exotic quantum states.

title: Polarization-based Indices In Quantum Many-body Systems: Validity And Extension Beyond One Dimension
authors: Yasuhiro Tada
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Tada

The expectation value of the twist operator has been widely used as a polarization-based index for gapped and gapless phases in interacting quantum many-body systems. Although numerous studies support this usage in specific settings, and rigorous results have established the validity of the criterio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235118] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polarization-based indices (twist operator expectation values) as order parameters for quantum many-body phases, extending their validity beyond one dimension.
motivation: Polarization-based indices are used to characterize gapped and gapless phases, but their validity in higher dimensions and for gapless systems is not fully established.
method: The author analytically and numerically examines the twist operator expectation value in various 2D models, including topological insulators and spin liquids, and compares with known topological invariants.
result: The twist operator index is shown to be a valid order parameter for certain 2D gapped phases but fails for some gapless systems; a modified index is proposed.
conclusion: Polarization-based indices can be extended beyond 1D but require careful interpretation; they are not universal order parameters for all many-body phases.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model and analytical/numerical methods to analyze the effects of slow defect dynamics on topological transitions.
result: They find that quenched disorder can modify the nature of topological transitions at finite temperature.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between disorder and topology in thermal systems.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a scalable tool for studying electronic structure in complex moiré materials.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Yusuke Miyajima And Masahito Mochizuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Miyajima and Masahito Mochizuki

Information-processing algorithms inspired by survival strategies of slime molds have been intensively studied to realize combinatorial optimization machines with high computational efficiency and low power consumption. However, previously proposed mathematical models are not suitable for physical i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023269] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A mathematical model for an amoeba-inspired combinatorial optimization machine is developed and shown to be equivalent to recurrent neural networks.
motivation: To enable physical implementation of slime mold-inspired optimization machines with high efficiency and low power consumption.
method: The authors propose a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is mathematically formulated and its equivalence to recurrent neural networks is established.
conclusion: The model provides a foundation for building physical optimization machines inspired by amoebas.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: Analytical and numerical study of quantum dimer models with specific domain geometries.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, leading to breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop a Pauli propagation technique to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise, leveraging noise-induced decay of non-stabilizer resources.
result: They prove that for typical circuits, local noise enables efficient classical simulation by suppressing magic and entanglement.
conclusion: Arbitrary local noise can render quantum circuits classically tractable, which has implications for noisy quantum computing and benchmarking.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits as a special class of lattices.
result: The paper presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems, drawing analogies with quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of switchable chiral magnons in the altermagnet MnTe using polarized inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly discovered class of magnetic materials with unique spin-split bands, and confirming the chirality of magnon modes is crucial for understanding their fundamental properties.
method: The authors performed polarized inelastic neutron scattering experiments on single-crystal MnTe to measure the magnon dispersion and determine the chirality of the split bands.
result: They provide the first unambiguous evidence of chirality in the split magnon bands of an altermagnet, demonstrating that the chirality can be switched by an external magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings establish altermagnets as a platform for studying chiral magnons and may have implications for spintronics and magnonics.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
authors: H. Maeda And K. Kitano
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods exist for cold atoms but not for thermal gases, limiting practical applications.
method: Exploits collective radiation from a thermal gas to achieve transverse-mode selection without a cavity.
result: Successfully demonstrates cavity-free mode control of superfluorescence in a thermal gas.
conclusion: Provides a new approach for light mode control that works with thermal gases, expanding possibilities for compact light sources.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of a metal hydride molecule (CaH), enabling production of ultracold atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride and then dissociating it offers a new route.
method: The authors laser-cool and trap calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules in a magneto-optical trap, using a repumping scheme to close the cooling cycle.
result: They achieve a trapped sample of CaH molecules at sub-millikelvin temperatures, demonstrating the first MOT of a metal hydride.
conclusion: This work opens the door to producing ultracold atomic hydrogen via dissociation of trapped CaH, which could benefit studies of fundamental physics and quantum gases.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee
abstract:
Author(s): A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, and F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: To understand how vibrational excitations affect electron transport at the atomic scale.
method: Atomic-scale measurements of electron transport in the presence of vibrational excitations.
result: Evidence of electron bunching mediated by atomic-scale vibrations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion, relevant for nanoscale electronics.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, and Jian-Ping Lv

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem via critical fluctuations.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems with only short-range interactions, which is forbidden by the Mermin-Wagner theorem in strictly 2D.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model with weak interlayer coupling.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperature, attributed to critical fluctuations that stabilize order despite short-range interactions.
conclusion: The quasi-2D XY model can exhibit long-range order, revising conventional understanding of phase transitions in low-dimensional systems.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Duilio De Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, and Eugene Demler

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a sequence of Bragg pulses to excite and probe nonlinear responses.
result: The method enables access to momentum-resolved nonlinear response functions, revealing dynamics beyond linear response.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold gases.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: To explore universal three-body physics in a novel system of shielded dipolar molecules, where anisotropic long-range interactions are present.
method: Quantum-mechanical three-body calculations using a model potential that accounts for microwave shielding and dipolar interactions.
result: Observation of Efimov resonances and universal scaling behavior despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction.
conclusion: Microwave-shielded polar molecules provide a new platform for studying Efimov physics and universal three-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
authors: Junyu Tang And Ran Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium by identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital motion does not generate a magnetic moment, making it challenging to define orbital angular momentum. The authors aim to formulate a proper theory for magnon OAM.
method: The authors identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM by considering the Aharonov-Casher effect and derive a continuity equation for the OAM density.
result: They obtain a consistent definition of magnon OAM that satisfies conservation laws and can be computed from equilibrium spin textures.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for magnon OAM, enabling future studies of orbital transport in magnetic insulators.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the core structure and topological phase transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze dislocation core structures and elastic properties in skyrmion lattices.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and topological phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the mechanics of skyrmion lattices beyond the traditional analogy.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales-type lattice defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a chiral spin liquid instability at finite defect density.
motivation: To understand how crystallographic defects affect the stability and phase diagram of the Kitaev spin liquid, which is a paradigmatic quantum spin liquid candidate.
method: The authors analyze the Kitaev model with odd-sided plaquettes introduced by Stone-Wales defects using analytical and numerical techniques, likely including mean-field or exact diagonalization.
result: A finite density of defects induces a finite-temperature phase transition to a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can qualitatively alter the physics of quantum spin liquids, potentially enabling new topological phases.

title: Boosting Gaussian Boson Sampling Using Optical Parametric Amplification Networks
authors: Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yukuan Zhao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) provides a route toward demonstrating quantum computational advantage. However, optical loss, which reduces the entanglement in the system, can render GBS results classically simulable. We propose a nonlinear photonic architecture based on optical parametric amplifiers …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062433] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonlinear photonic architecture using optical parametric amplifiers to boost Gaussian boson sampling performance under loss.
motivation: Optical loss in Gaussian boson sampling reduces entanglement and can make the output classically simulable, undermining claims of quantum advantage.
method: The authors design a network of optical parametric amplifiers integrated into the GBS setup to counteract loss and enhance non-classical correlations.
result: The proposed architecture improves the robustness of GBS against loss, potentially extending the regime where quantum advantage can be demonstrated.
conclusion: Optical parametric amplification networks offer a practical way to mitigate loss in GBS experiments, but the work is primarily an engineering solution rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals
authors: Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, And Jie-Yun Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, and Jie-Yun Yan

A conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) is designed to achieve highly efficient optical bistability. By exploiting the conjugate topological edge state supported by the CTPC, the structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold, reaching the level of a few microwatts per meter in …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063519] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates enhanced optical bistability in conjugate topological photonic crystals using topological edge states.
motivation: To achieve low-threshold optical bistability for applications in all-optical switching and signal processing.
method: Designs a conjugate topological photonic crystal (CTPC) that supports a topological edge state, and uses nonlinear optical effects to realize bistability.
result: The CTPC structure exhibits a markedly reduced bistability threshold down to a few microwatts per meter.
conclusion: Conjugate topological photonic crystals provide a promising platform for low-power optical bistability and nonlinear photonic devices.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient
authors: Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, And Le Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Bolong Jiao, Shuai Peng, Qinxuan Peng, Shaokun Liu, Mengde Gan, Jiaming Li, and Le Luo

We present a rapid evaporative cooling scheme for a strongly interacting [MATH] Fermi gas in an optical dipole trap. The method uses a magnetic-field-gradient-induced tilt of the trapping potential to accelerate cooling in the unitarity-limited regime. In evaporation based only on lowerin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; a faster method is needed to improve experimental efficiency.
method: A magnetic field gradient is applied to tilt the optical dipole trap, enhancing the escape of high-energy atoms and thus accelerating the evaporation process.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves significantly faster cooling rates compared to conventional evaporation, reaching quantum degeneracy in reduced time.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, with potential applications in quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, and Li-Gang Wang

The light deflection under a strong gravitational field, referred to as strong gravitational lensing, provides a powerful probe of spacetime geometry. Besides, laboratory analog models are employed to study the effects of curved spacetime and explore the design of optical devices. Here, applying the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing analogies in laboratory systems.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing effects using laboratory analog models and to design optical devices inspired by curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling of light propagation in an analog black hole setup, analyzing optical echoes and deflection.
result: They demonstrate that analog black holes can produce optical echoes similar to those expected in real gravitational lensing.
conclusion: Analog models provide a useful platform for studying gravitational lensing and may inspire novel optical devices.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
authors: Nicolò Piccione
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, focusing on optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to energy nonconservation and divergent heating rates in collapse models; smearing the mass density operator can regularize this, but the optimal smearing distribution is unknown.
method: The author derives conditions for minimal heating by analyzing the diffusion rate as a functional of the smearing distribution, using variational techniques.
result: An optimal smearing distribution is found that minimizes the heating rate, and the resulting diffusion is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a way to make collapse models phenomenologically viable by reducing predicted heating to testable levels.

title: Limitations Of An Approximative Phase-space Description In Strong-field Quantum Optics
authors: Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, And Christian Saugbjerg Lange
abstract:
Author(s): Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, and Christian Saugbjerg Lange

In recent years, strong-field processes such as high-order harmonic generation (HHG) and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical states of light have become an increasingly popular field of study. The theoretical modeling of these processes often applies an approximate phase-space expansio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063107] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the limitations of an approximate phase-space description in strong-field quantum optics, specifically for high-order harmonic generation and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical light.
motivation: Strong-field processes with nonclassical light are gaining interest, but theoretical models often rely on approximate phase-space expansions whose validity is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the accuracy of the phase-space expansion by comparing it to exact quantum calculations for specific strong-field scenarios.
result: They identify regimes where the approximation breaks down, providing quantitative bounds on its validity.
conclusion: The approximate phase-space description has limited applicability in strong-field quantum optics, and more accurate methods are needed for nonclassical driving fields.

title: Spin Chirality Driven Tunability And Multifunctionality In Two-dimensional Noncollinear Antiferromagnets
authors: Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, And Shixuan Du
abstract:
Author(s): Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, and Shixuan Du

Noncollinear antiferromagnets (NCAFs) offer an ideal platform for high-performance spintronic devices. Weak spin-orbit coupling (SOC) magnets, though abundant and important, are overlooked. We propose a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with [MATH] spin configur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin chirality and multifunctionality in two-dimensional noncollinear antiferromagnets, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for spintronics, but weak spin-orbit coupling magnets have been overlooked; the authors aim to propose a symmetry framework for such materials.
method: The authors develop a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with noncollinear spin configurations and analyze their electronic and magnetic properties.
result: They demonstrate tunable spin chirality and multifunctionality, including potential for spintronic devices.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for exploiting weak SOC magnets in spintronics, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Phase Transitions By Time-dependent Electromagnetic Fields In Frustrated Magnets: Role Of Dynamical And Static Magnetic Fields
authors: Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, And Satoru Hayami
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, and Satoru Hayami

We theoretically investigate the effects of time-dependent electromagnetic fields on frustrated magnets with the spatial inversion symmetry. Two types of external-field setups are considered. One is a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and the other is a combination of a circularly polarized…

tldr: The paper studies topological phase transitions in frustrated magnets driven by time-dependent electromagnetic fields, focusing on dynamical and static magnetic field effects.

method: Theoretical analysis using two external-field setups: a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and a combination of circularly polarized and static magnetic fields.
result: Identifies conditions for topological phase transitions and characterizes the resulting phases.
conclusion: Time-dependent electromagnetic fields can be used to control topological phases in frustrated magnets, offering a route to manipulate magnetic order.

Despite numerous recent studies on the Hall anomaly following the discovery of cuprate superconductivity, its origin remains contentious. We demonstrate—without invoking adjustable parameters—that a previously proposed mechanism, in which vacancies form within vortex lattice domains, provides a comp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214513] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a vacancy mechanism within vortex lattice domains to explain the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.
motivation: The Hall anomaly in mixed-state type-II superconductors remains contentious; the authors aim to resolve it without adjustable parameters.
method: They demonstrate that vacancies forming within vortex lattice domains can account for the Hall anomaly, using a previously proposed mechanism.
result: The mechanism provides a consistent explanation for the Hall anomaly without invoking adjustable parameters.
conclusion: Vacancies within vortex lattice domains are a plausible origin of the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.

result: They map the phase diagram of creation, repulsion, or annihilation of skyrmions upon absorption into a domain wall.

title: Hund's Coupling Governed Orbital-selective Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{K}}_{x}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, and Zhi-Xun Shen

While the influence of electronic correlations on superconductivity is a defining question, identifying how these correlations manifest in the superconducting state remains difficult. Furthermore, in multiorbital systems, correlations driven by Hund’s coupling can differentiate the behavior of individual orbitals, and how such orbital selectivity governs superconducting pairing has remained largely unexplored experimentally. Here, the authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to experimentally determine the superconducting gap of a representative iron-based superconductor as the Hund’s coupling influence increases. They find increased correlation diminishes the superconducting gap in an orbital-selective way, suggesting that Hund’s coupling plays a central role in shaping pairing in multiorbital superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224517] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ARPES to study orbital-selective superconductivity in Ba1-xKxFe2As2, finding that Hund's coupling governs the suppression of the superconducting gap in a correlation-dependent manner.
motivation: To understand how electronic correlations, particularly Hund's coupling, influence superconductivity in multiorbital systems, which remains experimentally unexplored.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the superconducting gap in Ba1-xKxFe2As2 as a function of doping, where Hund's coupling strength varies.
result: Increased correlation due to Hund's coupling diminishes the superconducting gap in an orbital-selective way, indicating that Hund's coupling shapes pairing in multiorbital superconductors.
conclusion: Hund's coupling plays a central role in orbital-selective superconductivity, providing insight into the interplay of correlations and pairing in iron-based superconductors.

motivation: To understand the physical manifestation of quantum geometry in momentum space and its relation to real-space structural geometry in flat band systems.
method: The authors analyze the quantum geometry of electronic states in singular flat bands and compute anomalous Landau level spreading using theoretical models.
result: They find that the interplay between quantum and real-space geometry leads to unique features in the Landau level spectrum of singular flat bands.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the geometric properties of flat bands and their observable consequences, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Three-dimensional Spin-orbital Liquids
authors: Anna Sandberg, Lukas Rødland, And Maria Hermanns
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Sandberg, Lukas Rødland, and Maria Hermanns

Here, the authors introduce exactly solvable three-dimensional spin–orbital liquids that generalize Kitaev models using multiple Majorana flavors. They show that these systems realize a unifying landscape of Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points, and show how symmetry and flavor mixing control their splitting, stability, and topological transitions. motivation: To understand gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions, which are less explored than their two-dimensional counterparts.
method: The authors construct exactly solvable models using multiple Majorana flavors and analyze their band structures, topological features, and symmetry properties.
result: They find a unifying landscape of Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points, and show how symmetry and flavor mixing control their splitting, stability, and topological transitions.
conclusion: This provides an organizing framework for gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions.

result: They observe structural phase separation and modulations in electrical transport.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of lattice distortions in electronic behavior, but the work is primarily materials science without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

conclusion: Twisted graphene systems can host chiral topological superconductivity, offering a platform for studying Majorana modes and topological quantum computation.

motivation: To understand how a quadratic well influences many-body dynamics, using an Ising chain as a model system.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field, examining time evolution and phase transitions.
result: The quadratic transverse field leads to periodic dynamics and modifies the quantum phase transition behavior compared to a uniform Ising chain.

conclusion: Hematite's magnonic properties make it a strong candidate for next-generation magnonic devices.

authors: Jan Biedermann And Lukas Janssen
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245123] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.

method: The authors analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using exclusion processes and resource constraints, likely via mean-field theory or simulations.
result: They observe emergent metastable states and characterize their properties under resource limitations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium steady states and metastability in networked transport systems.

title: Pearl Supratransmission In A Boundary-driven Two-dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With A Hole
authors: Rudy Kusdiantara And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Rudy Kusdiantara and Hadi Susanto

We investigate energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole. Harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation generates standing-wave states whose existence and stability depend on the driving amplitude, the inner radius, and the imposed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064204] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies energy supratransmission in a driven 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a hole, focusing on standing-wave states and stability.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave propagation and energy transfer in a 2D system with a defect, which is a problem in classical nonlinear dynamics.
method: Numerical simulation and stability analysis of the boundary-driven 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole and azimuthal modulation.
result: The existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on driving amplitude, inner radius, and azimuthal modulation.
conclusion: The study provides insights into supratransmission phenomena in 2D nonlinear systems with defects.

title: Community Detection By The Normalized Ricci Flow With The Optimization Of The Information Entropy
authors: Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, And Jiao Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, and Jiao Gu

Discrete Ricci curvature serves as a fundamental geometric tool for quantifying the structural characteristics of complex networks, effectively capturing the richness of their connection patterns. Building on this theoretical framework, this paper proposes an improved discrete Ricci curvature algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is important for understanding network structure, and discrete Ricci curvature provides a geometric tool to capture connectivity patterns.
method: The authors propose an improved discrete Ricci curvature algorithm and combine it with normalized Ricci flow and optimization of information entropy to detect communities.
result: The method is validated on synthetic and real-world networks, showing improved community detection performance compared to existing algorithms.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively leverages geometric and information-theoretic concepts for network analysis.

title: Dissipative Response Of Driven Bead-spring-dashpot Chains
authors: R. Kailasham
abstract:
Author(s): R. Kailasham

The work dissipated in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction is numerically calculated by considering a sequence of [MATH] spring-dashpots tethered at one end and being pulled at the other using a harmonic trap via linear and symmetric protocols. The variation of the dissipation with the chain…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065408] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the dissipated work in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction using a bead-spring-dashpot model.
motivation: Understanding dissipation in driven polymer chains is important for polymer physics and biophysics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors simulate a chain of spring-dashpots tethered at one end and pulled by a harmonic trap using linear and symmetric protocols, computing the work dissipated.
result: The variation of dissipation with chain length and pulling protocol is characterized numerically.
conclusion: The study provides insights into dissipative response of viscoelastic chains, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Controlling The Glass Transition Through Active Fluctuating Interactions
authors: Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, And Thibault Bertrand
abstract:
Author(s): Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, and Thibault Bertrand

Fluctuating pairwise interactions are understood to drive fluidlike states in dense biological systems. These states find a broad range of functionalities, such as directing growth during morphogenesis and forming aggregates with heightened mechanical response. However, a tractable model capturing t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062102] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how active fluctuating interactions control the glass transition in dense biological systems.
motivation: Understanding how fluidlike states arise in dense biological systems is important for morphogenesis and mechanical response.
method: The authors develop a tractable model of fluctuating pairwise interactions and analyze its effect on the glass transition.
result: They find that active fluctuations can drive the system into a fluidlike state, controlling the glass transition.
conclusion: Active fluctuating interactions provide a mechanism to tune the glass transition in biological materials.

title: Linearization Principle: The Geometric Origin Of Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Hiroki Suyari
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Suyari

Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in various complex systems. To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for these phenomena, we present a geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation by introducing the linearization principle directly at the dynamical st…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations via a linearization principle, aiming to provide a dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in many complex systems, but a consistent dynamical foundation is lacking.
method: The authors introduce a linearization principle directly at the dynamical level to derive nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations from a geometric perspective.
result: A geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations is provided, linking the linearization principle to the emergence of power-law distributions.
conclusion: The work offers a new geometric framework for understanding anomalous diffusion, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A mathematical model of anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To understand transport in complex media where diffusion is anomalous and influenced by external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions to model drift.
result: Derived expressions for mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics showing anomalous diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The model captures key features of anomalous diffusion under drift, relevant to physical and biological systems.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times in bosonic systems.
motivation: Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, hindering efficient measurement of observables.
method: The authors develop an exchange Monte Carlo algorithm tailored for continuous-space PIMC, enabling swaps between configurations at different temperatures.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces autocorrelation times and improves sampling efficiency for bosonic systems.
conclusion: Exchange Monte Carlo is an effective technique for accelerating PIMC simulations in continuous space, particularly for bosonic systems.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics techniques to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds that the critical temperature is bounded above by a universal number determined by the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks, a physical neural network model.
motivation: To understand how physical constraints affect learning dynamics and memory retention in neuromorphic systems.
method: The authors train differentiable resistor networks sequentially on multiple tasks and analyze forgetting behavior using Kirchhoff's laws.
result: They observe catastrophic forgetting similar to artificial neural networks, with some mitigation due to physical constraints.
conclusion: Physical neural networks face similar challenges in continual learning, suggesting the need for specialized algorithms.

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, and J. A. Plascak

The ferromagnetic spin-2 quantum Blume-Capel model in the presence of a transverse crystal field interaction is studied by employing a variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for the free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state. The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using variational methods and exact ground state mapping.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of a higher-spin quantum spin model with transverse crystal field.
method: A variational approach based on the Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state.
result: Thermodynamic properties are obtained, likely including phase diagrams and critical behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the quantum Blume-Capel model but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. At first, the transfer matrices are analyzed in three representations, i.e., Clifford algebraic representation, transfer …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical derivation of partition function and spontaneous magnetization for a 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
motivation: Extend the exactly solvable 2D Ising model to include next-nearest neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Transfer matrix method in Clifford algebraic representation and other representations.
result: Exact expressions for the partition function and spontaneous magnetization are derived.
conclusion: The model is exactly solvable, providing insights into phase transitions with extended interactions.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
authors: Arnau Vivet And Alex Arenas
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative gains and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence via a Lyapunov function.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models of associative memory, bridging neuroscience and machine learning.
method: Introduces a coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamical system with a Lyapunov function and entropy-regularized replicator equation for astrocytic gains.
result: The dynamics converge to fixed points that correspond to stored patterns, with self-attention-like behavior emerging from the astrocytic gating.
conclusion: The model provides a biologically plausible mechanism for attention in associative memory, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emulation Of Self-consistent non-Hermitian Quantum Formalisms
authors: Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, and R. Chitra

Hermiticity has long been a cornerstone of quantum theory, ensuring the conservation of probability and real energy spectra. Recent advances in non-Hermitian physics have revealed that this requirement can be relaxed, giving rise to richer dynamics where the Hilbert space is endowed with a time-depe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023271] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent non-Hermitian quantum formalism and demonstrates its emulation on a quantum computer.
motivation: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can describe open systems and gain/loss phenomena, but their probabilistic interpretation and simulation on quantum hardware remain challenging.
method: The authors propose a formalism that maps non-Hermitian dynamics to a dilated Hermitian system, enabling emulation on a quantum processor via a variational algorithm.
result: They successfully emulate non-Hermitian dynamics for small systems on a quantum computer, showing agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway to simulate non-Hermitian quantum systems on near-term quantum devices, expanding the scope of quantum simulation.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, specifically the Mott transition, and to explore analogies between classical and quantum critical phenomena.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities such as specific heat and compressibility near the critical endpoint of the Mott transition, comparing them to the Frenkel line behavior in classical fluids.
result: They identify a line of maxima in thermodynamic response functions analogous to the Frenkel line, suggesting a crossover rather than a sharp phase transition in the pseudogap region.
conclusion: The analogy provides a unified framework for understanding crossover phenomena in both classical and quantum fluids, but the work is primarily a theoretical/computational study in condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unveiling Dielectric Relaxation And Shear Rheology In Water
authors: Songming Liu And Jiaxing Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Songming Liu and Jiaxing Yuan

The complex dynamics of liquid water are manifested in its unique dielectric relaxation and nonlinear shear rheology. We investigate the dielectric and rheological responses of TIP4P/[MATH] water using molecular dynamics simulations across a wide temperature range, including the deeply supercooled regi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023266] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of dielectric relaxation and shear rheology in water using TIP4P model.
motivation: To understand the complex dynamics of liquid water, especially in the deeply supercooled regime.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P water across a wide temperature range.
result: Characterization of dielectric and rheological responses.
conclusion: Provides insights into water's dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: To leverage noisy near-term quantum devices for quantum chemistry by reducing the required quantum resources and mitigating noise.
method: Uses a quantum computer to prepare an approximate ground state and measure Hamiltonian matrix elements in a subspace of configurations, then classically diagonalizes the resulting small Hamiltonian.
result: Demonstrates accurate energy estimates for small molecules with fewer quantum operations than full quantum phase estimation.
conclusion: The approach is a practical hybrid algorithm that can run on noisy quantum devices and improve quantum chemistry calculations.

title: Trapping And Cooling Mechanisms In Blue-detuned Magneto-optical Traps Of Molecules
authors: Qinshu Lyu And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): Qinshu Lyu and M. R. Tarbutt

This work identifies the mechanisms responsible for trapping and cooling in a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap driven by a pair of closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization. When the Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference between the two components, there is a state that is dark to the beam propagating in one direction but not to the beam from the opposite direction, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023259] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trapping and cooling mechanisms in blue-detuned magneto-optical traps for molecules, focusing on radiation pressure forces from two-frequency components.
motivation: Understanding and improving laser cooling and trapping of molecules is important for precision measurements and quantum science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap with two closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization, identifying a dark state mechanism that generates a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.
result: They identify the trapping and cooling mechanisms, showing how Zeeman splitting matching the frequency difference creates direction-dependent dark states that produce a confining force.
conclusion: The work provides insight into molecular magneto-optical trapping but is purely atomic/molecular physics with no direct relevance to the user's research directions.

title: Update Of Hartree-Fock Theory For Hubbard-like Models
authors: E. Langmann And J. Lenells
abstract:
Author(s): E. Langmann and J. Lenells

We show that the standard textbook description of (restricted) Hartree-Fock theory for (Fermi) Hubbard-like models is in need of an update, and we present such an update allowing us to correct basic and established results in the condensed matter physics literature that are qualitatively wrong. Our …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023262] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper corrects Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models, revealing qualitative errors in established condensed matter results.
motivation: Standard textbook Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard models yields qualitatively wrong results; an updated formulation is needed.
method: The authors present a revised restricted Hartree-Fock approach that properly accounts for the on-site interaction term in Hubbard-like models.
result: The corrected theory resolves discrepancies and provides accurate mean-field descriptions for these models.
conclusion: The updated Hartree-Fock theory should replace the standard textbook treatment for Hubbard-like models in condensed matter physics.

title: Quantum-enhanced T-stochastic Neighbor Embedding For High-dimensional Data Visualization
authors: Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, And Song Lin
abstract:
