Author(s): Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, and Song Lin

t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) is a nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm that preserves local similarity by matching probability distributions between high- and low-dimensional spaces. Owing to its ability to capture complex manifold structures, t-SNE has become a widely…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023265] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced version of t-SNE for high-dimensional data visualization using quantum amplitude estimation.
motivation: Classical t-SNE is computationally expensive for large datasets; quantum computing may offer speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages amplitude estimation to accelerate the computation of pairwise similarities and gradient descent in t-SNE.
result: The quantum-enhanced t-SNE achieves a quadratic speedup in the number of data points compared to classical t-SNE.
conclusion: Quantum algorithms can improve dimensionality reduction for data visualization, but practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Effects Of Berry Curvature On Ideal Fractional Chern Insulator Many-body Gaps
authors: Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, And Nicolás Morales-Durán
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, and Nicolás Morales-Durán

This work studies ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands relevant to semiconductor moiré materials. It shows how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in favor of charge density waves and explains this mechanism using the single-mode approximation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022045] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in moiré materials, favoring charge density waves.
motivation: Understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in realistic materials is crucial for realizing topological phases, but Berry curvature inhomogeneity can disrupt these states.
method: The authors analyze ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands using the single-mode approximation to study the effect of Berry curvature variations on many-body gaps.
result: Berry curvature inhomogeneity reduces the gap for fractional Chern insulators and can induce a transition to charge density wave order.
conclusion: Berry curvature inhomogeneity is a key factor limiting fractional Chern insulator stability, and its control is necessary for experimental realization.

title: Dynamic Similarity Of Vortex Shedding In A Superfluid Flowing Past A Penetrable Obstacle
authors: Junhwan Kwon And Yong-Il Shin
abstract:
Author(s): Junhwan Kwon and Yong-il Shin

We numerically investigate wake dynamics in a superfluid flowing past a penetrable obstacle. The penetrable obstacle does not fully deplete the density, and we define an effective diameter [MATH] from the Mach-1 contour of the time-averaged irrotational flow around the obstacle, which …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023246] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of vortex shedding dynamics in a superfluid flowing past a penetrable obstacle, focusing on dynamic similarity and effective diameter scaling.
motivation: Understanding wake dynamics in superfluids is important for fundamental fluid dynamics and potential applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a superfluid flow past a penetrable obstacle, analyzing vortex shedding patterns and defining an effective diameter from the Mach-1 contour.
result: The vortex shedding frequency scales with the effective diameter, showing dynamic similarity analogous to classical fluids.
conclusion: The penetrable obstacle can be characterized by an effective diameter that captures the essential wake dynamics, extending classical similarity concepts to superfluids.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs via numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate that the fuzzy sphere can accurately capture the critical properties of free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and observe emergent supersymmetry in certain interacting models.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach for studying fermionic CFTs, with potential applications to more complex strongly coupled theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, demonstrating three distinct magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2 and establishing a framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices, which are of interest for information manipulation via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures in EuAg4Sb2, combined with theoretical modeling to identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are revealed in EuAg4Sb2, providing a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work establishes a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures, with potential applications in spintronics and information storage.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps under thermal fluctuations for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial for predicting system behavior, but existing methods often lack a physical basis.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of networked dynamical systems.
result: The framework accurately predicts physical links across various network dynamics, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed causal inference provides a robust approach for uncovering interaction structures in complex networks.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting diodes, which is important for low-dissipation electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect without breaking time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents without an external magnetic field.
conclusion: This work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diodes in gate-defined homojunctions, with potential applications in superconducting electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers at topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers beyond conventional exciton condensation.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological criticality and anyon physics in quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton superfluids with robust properties.
conclusion: Provides a mechanism for engineering anyonic superfluids in quantum Hall systems.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering under applied electric fields.
result: The experiments reveal a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and show electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in statistical physics and soft matter, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and how this affects the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal novel critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to statistical mechanics but not to the user's research interests.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a bulk insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between multiple ferroic orders and the formation of complex domain walls in a material with a uniform ferro-rotational state.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to identify and analyze the polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in Ni₃TeO₆.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for multifunctional materials.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling spin-based devices.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene heterostructures to observe gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of spin-dependent electron focusing and a ballistic spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can support coherent spin transport and spin control through electron optics, promising for spintronics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering, and understanding the nematic state is key to their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical condensed matter techniques to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: Identification and characterization of a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The nematic ordering is fundamental to relaxor ferroelectric behavior.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for novel electronic phases.
method: Combines resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and ultrafast optical spectroscopy to probe excitations across equilibrium and hidden states.
result: Identifies unique polaronic and phononic excitations in the hidden phase that are absent in equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can create long-lived hidden phases with distinct lattice and electronic excitations, offering a pathway to control material properties.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: Increasing activity can counterintuitively reduce the solid's active response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The percolation threshold governs the macroscopic active response, leading to a 'more is less' effect.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to provide an end-to-end implementation on current quantum hardware.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithm pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the approximation of the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and analyzing resource requirements.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose target states into a sequence of elementary operations, including photon catalysis and linear optics.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical pathway for photonic quantum state preparation, though it does not directly address the user's core research directions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: The paper is a review, synthesizing results from many experimental and theoretical studies.
result: It covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving and opening new directions for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses serve as a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is relevant to many areas of physics.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical developments, and large-scale numerical simulations to track progress in the field.
result: The paper highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation, and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with ongoing challenges and applications across physics.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic phases of matter with potential applications in topological quantum computing, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review summarizes theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental progress in candidate materials.
result: Highlights key materials and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview for researchers in quantum spin liquids, but is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: A review applying statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze simultaneous recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations, bridging statistical physics and neuroscience.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from statistical physics can achieve predictive power in studying brain activity.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open challenges in modeling internal conversion in complex systems.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to accurately predict internal conversion rates, which will aid in designing better photonic and energy-harvesting materials.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential for spintronic applications.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum effects, including quantum tunneling, entanglement, and interactions.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum skyrmion physics, such as quantum depinning and skyrmion qubits.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for quantum technologies, but many open questions remain.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them.
result: Summarizes current constraints on various spin-dependent interactions and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential to reveal new physics, but no definitive discovery has been made.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions using atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems in atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
result: Summarizes current progress and challenges in engineering synthetic quantum matter with exotic geometries.
conclusion: These platforms offer new avenues for quantum simulation but are not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects like decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as sensitive probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts to detect gravity-induced decoherence, collapse, and entanglement in massive quantum systems.
result: Summarizes current state-of-the-art experiments and theoretical models for testing quantum gravity effects with massive particles.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further experimental and theoretical work is needed.

title: Room-Temperature Intrinsic Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect In ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, And Faxian Xiu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, and Faxian Xiu

A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236302] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe4 at room temperature, driven by a Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
motivation: To explore nonlinear transport phenomena in topological semimetals and understand the role of Berry curvature in generating nonlinear Hall effects without magnetic ordering.
method: Experimental measurement of the nonlinear planar Hall effect in TaIrTe4 under an in-plane magnetic field, combined with theoretical analysis based on Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
result: A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect is observed, attributed to an orbital mechanism involving the Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new mechanism for nonlinear Hall effects in nonmagnetic topological materials, with potential applications in rectification and frequency doubling.

title: Crystal-Field-Tuned Spin-Flip Luminescence In ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, And Abhay Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, and Abhay Shukla

Layered magnetic materials provide the opportunity for fundamental investigations of magnetism in the two-dimensional limit. [MATH], a prototype member of this family, is antiferromagnetic below 155 K and exhibits sharp photoluminescence associated with a transition between a triplet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236401] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal-field-tuned spin-flip luminescence in the layered antiferromagnet NiPS3, focusing on its optical and magnetic properties.
motivation: Layered magnetic materials like NiPS3 are of interest for fundamental studies of 2D magnetism, and understanding their photoluminescence can reveal spin dynamics and crystal field effects.
method: The authors perform photoluminescence spectroscopy under varying crystal fields (e.g., via pressure or doping) and analyze the spin-flip transition features.
result: They observe that the spin-flip luminescence is tunable by crystal field modifications, with changes in emission energy and intensity correlated with magnetic ordering.
conclusion: Crystal field engineering can control spin-flip luminescence in NiPS3, providing a route to manipulate optical and magnetic properties in 2D magnets.

title: Role Of Anionic Lone-Pair-Like Electrons In Producing Minimum Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, And Zhigang Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, and Zhigang Zou

Cationic lone-pair electrons are often associated with distinctive phonon properties (e.g., strong lattice anharmonicity) that lead to low lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]). However, the reliance on specific cations (e.g., [MATH] or [MATH]) severely restri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236301] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the role of anionic lone-pair-like electrons in achieving minimum lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectric materials.
motivation: To overcome the limitation of relying on specific cations for low lattice thermal conductivity by exploring anionic lone-pair-like electrons.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental measurements to analyze phonon properties and thermal conductivity.
result: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons induce strong lattice anharmonicity, leading to ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons provide a new strategy for designing materials with minimum lattice thermal conductivity.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, and Michele Ceriotti

Machine learning can reduce the number of time steps needed to accurately predict the progress of a dynamically evolving system.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by learning the action for long time steps.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations require many small time steps for accuracy, which is computationally expensive. The authors aim to reduce the number of steps by learning a surrogate model that can predict system evolution over longer intervals.
method: They propose a machine learning approach to learn the action (a time-integrated quantity) of the dynamical system, enabling larger time steps while maintaining accuracy.
result: The method demonstrates significant speedup in molecular dynamics simulations with controlled error, as validated on benchmark systems.
conclusion: Learning the action via machine learning is a promising strategy to accelerate molecular dynamics, though it may require careful tuning for different systems.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
authors: Raymond Isichei And João Magueijo
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

We show that general relativity and other geometrical theories can be viewed as a degenerate Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs in emergent gravity. Including work-producing legs yields controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation, which produce late-time c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231501] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity and studies Lorentz violation from work-producing legs.
motivation: To explore controlled violations of Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation within an emergent gravity framework.
method: Models gravity as a thermodynamic Otto cycle with heat-exchange legs, then adds work-producing legs to generate Lorentz violations.
result: Lorentz violation and energy-momentum non-conservation emerge at late times, with cosmological consequences.
conclusion: The emergent gravity perspective can produce testable Lorentz violations, linking thermodynamics to gravity.

title: Alternative Representation Of Multichannel Rydberg Spectra: A Modified $K$-matrix And Lu-Fano Plot Applied To The Manganese Spectroscopy
authors: Justin D. Piel And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Justin D. Piel and Chris H. Greene

The well-known graphical representation called the Lu-Fano plot was originally developed for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy, especially in quantum-defect theory. The present study shows some of the limitations of this traditional Lu-Fano plot that are desirable to improve on, when there are close…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062805] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a modified K-matrix and Lu-Fano plot for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy in manganese.
motivation: Traditional Lu-Fano plots have limitations when there are close channels; the authors aim to improve the graphical representation.
method: They introduce an alternative representation using a modified K-matrix and a new Lu-Fano plot.
result: The modified approach addresses limitations of the traditional plot and is applied to manganese spectroscopy.
conclusion: The new representation offers a more effective tool for analyzing multichannel Rydberg spectra.

title: Th:SBO Single Crystal: A Multifunction Material For Solid-state Nuclear Optical Clocks
authors: Lin Li, Qiaorui Gong, Yuxiang Li, Runzhe Yang, Guoliang Deng, Shanming Li, Peixiong Zhang, Chengchun Zhao, Yin Hang, Longsheng Ma, And Shining Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Li, Qiaorui Gong, Yuxiang Li, Runzhe Yang, Guoliang Deng, Shanming Li, Peixiong Zhang, Chengchun Zhao, Yin Hang, Longsheng Ma, and Shining Zhu

The authors grow thorium-doped strontium tetraborate (Th:SBO) single crystals via the Czochralski method and characterize their structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties. The Th:SBO crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable a dual-functional platform that integrates nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060801] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the growth and characterization of thorium-doped strontium tetraborate (Th:SBO) single crystals for potential use in solid-state nuclear optical clocks.
motivation: To develop a dual-functional platform that combines nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host for nuclear optical clock applications.
method: Th:SBO single crystals were grown via the Czochralski method, and their structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties were characterized.
result: The Th:SBO crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable integration of nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host.
conclusion: Th:SBO is a promising multifunctional material for solid-state nuclear optical clocks, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: Demonstration Of An Interferometric Technique For Measuring Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence With An Optical Cavity
authors: Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, And Laura Roberts
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, and Laura Roberts

Vacuum magnetic birefringence (VMB) is an effect predicted by quantum electrodynamics in which the vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium and exhibits a birefringence in the presence of a magnetic field. In this work, an interferometric scheme is introduced to measure this effect by sensing th…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063518] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an interferometric technique to measure vacuum magnetic birefringence, a QED effect, using an optical cavity.
motivation: Vacuum magnetic birefringence is a predicted QED effect that has not been directly observed; measuring it would test fundamental physics.
method: The authors use an optical cavity to enhance the signal and an interferometric scheme to detect the tiny birefringence induced by a magnetic field.
result: They present a proof-of-principle demonstration and sensitivity analysis, showing the technique can reach the required precision.
conclusion: The interferometric cavity technique is a promising approach for detecting vacuum magnetic birefringence, potentially enabling the first direct measurement.

title: Fermi Surface And Topology Of The Multiband Superconductor BeAu
authors: Riccardo Vocaturo, Klaus Koepernik, Dániel Varjas, Oleg Janson, Maia G. Vergniory, And Jeroen van Den Brink
abstract:
Author(s): Riccardo Vocaturo, Klaus Koepernik, Dániel Varjas, Oleg Janson, Maia G. Vergniory, and Jeroen van den Brink

The chiral material BeAu was recently identified as a multiband type-I superconductor with a critical temperature of 3.2 K. As a member of the B20 crystal family (space group [MATH]), its band structure hosts multifold fermions at high-symmetry points, unpaired WPs, and even nodal surfaces. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224518] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Fermi surface and topological properties of the multiband superconductor BeAu using DFT and tight-binding modeling.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and topological features of BeAu, a recently discovered type-I superconductor with chiral B20 structure.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and tight-binding modeling to compute band structure, Fermi surface, and topological invariants.
result: Identifies multifold fermions, unpaired Weyl points, and nodal surfaces in the band structure; analyzes the Fermi surface topology.
conclusion: BeAu exhibits rich topological features that may influence its superconducting properties, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is established.

title: Singular Value Decomposition To Describe Bound States In The Continuum In Periodic Metasurfaces
authors: Nikita Ustimenko, Ivan Fernandez-Corbaton, And Carsten Rockstuhl
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Ustimenko, Ivan Fernandez-Corbaton, and Carsten Rockstuhl

Understanding how bound states in the continuum (BICs) emerge in periodic metasurfaces is essential for the controlled design of high-[MATH] resonances and their systematic manipulation. Here, we investigate the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the effective transition matrix and the scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235418] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses singular value decomposition to analyze bound states in the continuum in periodic metasurfaces, focusing on electromagnetic scattering.
motivation: Understanding how bound states in the continuum emerge in periodic metasurfaces is essential for designing high-Q resonances.
method: The authors apply singular value decomposition to the effective transition matrix and scattering matrix of periodic metasurfaces.
result: The SVD reveals the formation of BICs and their properties in the scattering response.
conclusion: The SVD approach provides a systematic way to describe and manipulate BICs in metasurfaces.

title: Electric Field And Nonvolatile Ferroelectric Driven Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetism In A ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$ Monolayer MXene
authors: Yuqian Yu, Xueyi Lian, Dingwen Zhang, Haoshen Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Leiming Chen, G. P. Zhang, And Jianli Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuqian Yu, Xueyi Lian, Dingwen Zhang, Haoshen Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Leiming Chen, G. P. Zhang, and Jianli Wang

Fully compensated ferrimagnets possess the advantages of both collinear compensated net magnetic moments and nonrelativistic spin splitting in which the nonvolatile control is a prerequisite for realizing the spintronic nanodevices. The A-type antiferromagnetic MXene is a potential candidate for the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245417] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric field control of fully compensated ferrimagnetism in a Cr2O3 monolayer MXene for spintronic applications.
motivation: To achieve nonvolatile control of fully compensated ferrimagnets, which are promising for spintronic nanodevices due to their compensated net magnetic moments and nonrelativistic spin splitting.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of Cr2O3 monolayer MXene under electric fields and ferroelectric polarization.
result: Electric fields and ferroelectric polarization can induce and control fully compensated ferrimagnetism in the Cr2O3 monolayer.
conclusion: The Cr2O3 monolayer MXene is a potential platform for voltage-controlled spintronic devices.

title: Ultrafast X-ray Thermometry: Contrasting Strain And Debye-Waller Effects In Platinum Thin Films
authors: J.-E. Pudell, M. Mattern, F. Baltrusch, F. L. Boariu, M. Kronseder, R. Shayduk, A. Madsen, M. Rössle, M. Bargheer, D. Schick, And A. von Reppert
abstract:
Author(s): J.-E. Pudell, M. Mattern, F. Baltrusch, F. L. Boariu, M. Kronseder, R. Shayduk, A. Madsen, M. Rössle, M. Bargheer, D. Schick, and A. von Reppert

Thermal energy and temperature govern a wide range of physical properties and dynamics in solids. X-ray diffraction can be used to monitor material-specific temperatures on ultrafast timescales and within nanostructures by exploiting thermal expansion or the Debye-Waller effect. Here, we simultaneou…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220301] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ultrafast X-ray diffraction to measure temperature in platinum thin films by separating strain and Debye-Waller effects.
motivation: To develop a method for ultrafast thermometry in nanostructures, which is important for understanding heat transport and dynamics in materials.
method: Simultaneous analysis of X-ray diffraction peak shifts (strain) and intensity changes (Debye-Waller effect) to extract temperature, supported by simulations.
result: The two effects can be disentangled to yield accurate temperature profiles on picosecond timescales.
conclusion: The approach provides a reliable ultrafast thermometer for thin films, with potential applications in nanoscale heat management.

title: Nonlinear Breakdown Of Antisymmetric Flexoelectric Coupling
authors: Yingzhuo Lun, Yida Yang, Tingjun Wang, Qi Ren, Sang-Wook Cheong, Xueyun Wang, And Jiawang Hong
abstract:
Author(s): Yingzhuo Lun, Yida Yang, Tingjun Wang, Qi Ren, Sang-Wook Cheong, Xueyun Wang, and Jiawang Hong

Flexoelectric coupling is conventionally regarded as antisymmetric, such that reversing the strain gradient reverses the polarization direction while preserving its magnitude. Here we report that this antisymmetric coupling breaks down in noncentrosymmetric single crystals driven by large strain gra…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214104] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a nonlinear breakdown of antisymmetric flexoelectric coupling in noncentrosymmetric single crystals under large strain gradients.
motivation: Flexoelectric coupling is conventionally antisymmetric; this work investigates deviations from this behavior under large strain gradients.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis on noncentrosymmetric single crystals subjected to large strain gradients.
result: The antisymmetric coupling breaks down, leading to nonlinear polarization responses.
conclusion: The findings challenge the conventional antisymmetric assumption and have implications for flexoelectric device design.

title: Large Inverse Magnetocaloric Effect Induced By Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction In Two-dimensional Ferromagnetic Semiconductors
authors: Guangwei Zhai, Chang Niu, Min Li, Xiong Xu, And Hui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Guangwei Zhai, Chang Niu, Min Li, Xiong Xu, and Hui Wang

Two-dimensional magnets have emerged as a promising platform for nanoscale spintronics and solid-state refrigeration. In this work, we investigate the magnetic phase transitions and magnetocaloric properties of monolayer [MATH] [MATH] using density functional …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245202] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetocaloric effect in a 2D ferromagnetic semiconductor driven by Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction using DFT.
motivation: To explore the potential of 2D magnets for nanoscale spintronics and solid-state refrigeration.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate magnetic phase transitions and magnetocaloric properties.
result: A large inverse magnetocaloric effect is induced by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
conclusion: The findings suggest that 2D ferromagnetic semiconductors with DMI could be promising for magnetocaloric cooling applications.

title: Tunable Optical Spin Hall Effect In An Open Cavity
authors: Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, and Zhanghai Chen

The optical spin Hall effect (OSHE), resulting from photonic spin-orbit coupling, has become a pivotal phenomenon in nanophotonics. While a tunable optical spin Hall effect has been achieved in liquid-crystal-based anisotropic microcavities, a more general material-independent and broadband platform…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245416] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a tunable optical spin Hall effect in an open cavity, enabling broadband and material-independent control of photonic spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: The optical spin Hall effect is important for nanophotonics, but existing platforms are limited to specific materials like liquid crystals. A more general, tunable platform is desired.
method: The authors use an open cavity structure to achieve tunable spin-orbit coupling, allowing control over the optical spin Hall effect via cavity parameters.
result: They experimentally demonstrate tunable spin splitting and spin-dependent beam shifts, with broadband operation and material independence.
conclusion: The open cavity platform provides a versatile and tunable approach to the optical spin Hall effect, with potential applications in photonic devices.

title: Phonon-mediated Thermal Transport In Two-dimensional ${\mathrm{MoSe}}_{2}$ At Cryogenic Temperatures From Accelerated ab Initio Calculations
authors: Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Shao, And Hua Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Shao, and Hua Bao

Understanding thermal transport in two-dimensional (2D) materials at cryogenic temperatures is essential for emerging low-temperature nanoelectronics, yet remains largely unexplored because of the lack of a predictive theoretical framework. Here, we develop a rigorous, accelerated, mode-resolved fir…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214309] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated thermal transport in 2D MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures using accelerated ab initio calculations.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in 2D materials at cryogenic temperatures is important for low-temperature nanoelectronics but lacks a predictive theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a rigorous, accelerated, mode-resolved first-principles approach to compute thermal conductivity.
result: They obtain mode-resolved thermal transport properties of monolayer MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting thermal transport in 2D materials at low temperatures, relevant for nanoelectronics.

title: Dynamics And Pinning For Skyrmions In Altermagnets
authors: J. C. Bellizotti Souza, C. J. O. Reichhardt, A. Saxena, And C. Reichhardt
abstract:
Author(s): J. C. Bellizotti Souza, C. J. O. Reichhardt, A. Saxena, and C. Reichhardt

We examine the dynamics, Hall angle, and pinning for Néel skyrmions in an altermagnet. Using an atomistic model, we show that skyrmion velocity and Hall angle dependence are anisotropic with respect to the direction of the drive, due to the fourfold symmetry implied by the two sublattices of the alt…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224424] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics and pinning of skyrmions in altermagnets, focusing on anisotropic velocity and Hall angle effects.
motivation: Understanding skyrmion motion in altermagnets is important for potential spintronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use an atomistic model to simulate Néel skyrmions in an altermagnet with two sublattices, analyzing velocity and Hall angle as functions of drive direction.
result: Skyrmion velocity and Hall angle exhibit strong anisotropy due to the fourfold symmetry of the altermagnet, and pinning effects are characterized.
conclusion: The work provides insights into skyrmion dynamics in altermagnets but is purely classical condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamic relevance.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijit Bera and Kevin E. Bassler

Variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) are a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes that unify a broad range of previously studied models within a single parametrized framework. Their dynamics consist of discrete random steps, or flights, during which the walker's speed varies…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, a class of stochastic processes.
motivation: To unify and understand a broad range of anomalous diffusion models within a single parametrized framework.
method: The authors analyze variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) using a decomposition approach that separates the process into components.
result: They achieve a complete decomposition of the anomalous diffusion behavior, characterizing the contributions of different flight segments.
conclusion: The work provides a unified theoretical framework for anomalous diffusion, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chromatic Percolation In Two-dimensional Multitype Particle Systems With Extended-range Homotypic Repulsion
authors: Tingting Yin, Yan Sui, Xueying Yuan, And Xian Kong
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Yin, Yan Sui, Xueying Yuan, and Xian Kong

Cells in many tissues repel like neighbors over extended ranges, yet standard jamming models ignore this diversity. We introduce chromatic percolation—the percolation of like-type particles driven by extended-range homotypic repulsion in multitype assemblies—and map its relation to mechanical jammin…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065412] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A study of percolation and jamming in multitype particle systems with extended-range homotypic repulsion, using a model called chromatic percolation.
motivation: To understand how extended-range homotypic repulsion affects percolation and mechanical jamming in diverse cell assemblies, which is relevant to tissue biology.
method: The authors introduce chromatic percolation, a percolation model for like-type particles with extended-range repulsion, and analyze it via simulations and theoretical mapping to jamming.
result: They find that extended-range homotypic repulsion can induce chromatic percolation transitions that are correlated with mechanical jamming.
conclusion: The work provides a framework linking percolation and jamming in multitype systems, with implications for understanding tissue mechanics.

title: Entropic Clustering Of Stickers Induces Aging In Biocondensates
authors: Hugo Le Roy And Paolo de Los Rios
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Le Roy and Paolo De Los Rios

Biomolecular condensates are cellular phase-separated droplets that usually exhibit a viscoelastic mechanical response, a behavior rationalized by modeling the complex molecules that make up a condensate as stickers and spacers, which assemble into a network-like structure. Condensates usually exhib…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064405] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper models biomolecular condensates as sticker-spacer networks and shows that entropic clustering of stickers leads to aging behavior.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates exhibit viscoelastic mechanical response, which is not fully understood. The authors aim to explain aging in these systems using a minimal model.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stickers and spacers, where stickers form reversible crosslinks. They analyze the dynamics using a master equation and Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They find that entropic clustering of stickers causes the system to age, with the relaxation time increasing over time, consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: The model captures the aging behavior of biocondensates, suggesting that entropic effects play a key role in their mechanical properties.

title: Further Testing The Validity Of Generalized Heterogeneous-elasticity Theory For Low-frequency Excitations In Structural Glasses
authors: Walter Schirmacher, Matteo Paoluzzi, Felix Cosmin Mocanu, Dmytro Khomenko, Grzegorz Szamel, Francesco Zamponi, And Giancarlo Ruocco

tldr: This paper tests the validity of generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory for low-frequency excitations in structural glasses, focusing on nonuniversal scaling of the vibrational density of states.
motivation: Understanding low-frequency vibrational excitations in glasses is important for explaining their thermal and mechanical properties, but the universality of the scaling law is debated.
method: The authors summarize their previous theory and provide further computational evidence by analyzing the nonphononic vibrational density of states in model glasses.
result: They demonstrate nonuniversality of the ω^4 scaling of the nonphononic density of states, supporting their generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory.
conclusion: The findings confirm that low-frequency excitations in glasses are not universal and depend on microscopic details, validating the proposed theory.

title: Diffusion-driven Pattern Formation In An Opinion Dynamical Network Model
authors: Tim Mauch And Thilo Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Mauch and Thilo Gross

The spatial organization of individuals and their interactions in communities are important factors known to preserve diversity in many complex systems. Inspired by metapopulation models from ecology, we study opinion formation using a network-based approach in which nodes represent communities of i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion formation using a network-based metapopulation model, focusing on spatial pattern formation and diversity preservation.
motivation: Understanding how spatial organization and network structure influence opinion diversity in complex social systems.
method: A network model where nodes represent communities with internal dynamics, coupled via migration-like interactions, analyzed using linear stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: The model exhibits diffusion-driven pattern formation, leading to spatially heterogeneous opinion states that can preserve diversity.
conclusion: Spatial coupling and network topology can sustain opinion diversity, analogous to ecological metapopulation dynamics.

title: Minority Takeover In Majority Dynamics: Searching For Rare Initializations Via The History Passing Algorithm
authors: Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, And Lenka Zdeborová
abstract:

Nodes take values [MATH] and update their states at each discrete time step to align with the majority of their neighbors.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies majority dynamics on random regular graphs, focusing on the minimal bias needed for a minority to take over, using a history passing algorithm.
motivation: Understanding how initial conditions affect global consensus in deterministic majority dynamics on large random graphs.
method: The authors analyze synchronous deterministic majority dynamics on random d-regular graphs and propose a history passing algorithm to search for rare initial configurations that lead to minority takeover.
result: They find that a small bias in the initial configuration can cause the minority to become the majority, and characterize the threshold bias as a function of graph degree.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the sensitivity of majority dynamics to initial conditions, with implications for social dynamics and distributed computing.

title: Free-energy Model Of Ferroelectric Transition In P(VDF-TrFE) Copolymer
authors: Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, And Vadim I. Sultanov
abstract:

We develop a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in poly(vinylidene difluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) [P(VDF-TrFE)] copolymers. The low-temperature ferroelectric phase is an orthorhombic crystal analogous to the poly(vinylidene difluoride) β-phase, wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065405] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Develops a free-energy model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.
motivation: To understand the phase transition in a technologically relevant ferroelectric polymer.
method: Constructs a physics-based analytical free-energy model incorporating dipole interactions and chain conformations.
result: The model reproduces the first-order phase transition and predicts the temperature dependence of polarization.
conclusion: The model provides a quantitative description of the ferroelectric transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz

tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM were not well understood; the authors aimed to explain this phenomenon.
method: The authors performed HR-TEM image simulations that include correlated atom vibrations to model the effect of phonon edge modes.
result: The simulations account for the observed enhanced vibrations, confirming the presence of localized phonon edge states.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes are responsible for the enhanced atomic vibrations at edges of MoS2, providing insight into edge effects in 2D materials.

title: Dynamical Learning In Deep Asymmetric Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, And Riccardo Zecchina
