[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023281] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical learning in asymmetric recurrent neural networks, focusing on the emergence of stable configuration manifolds.
motivation: To understand how asymmetric interactions and self-couplings in recurrent neural networks can lead to complex dynamical behaviors and learning.
method: The authors analyze recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions, incorporating self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections, and study the resulting dynamical properties.
result: They find that such networks develop a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations, which enhances learning and representation capacity.
conclusion: Asymmetric recurrent neural networks with appropriate couplings can exhibit rich dynamics beneficial for learning, with potential implications for understanding neural computation.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Observation of an amplitude-like mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for macroscopic quantum condensation and collective excitations; identifying collective modes is key to understanding their physics.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode in Ta2Pd3Te5.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitude-like mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for collective excitations in excitonic insulators, advancing the understanding of these quantum materials.

title: Reducibility Of Higher-order To Pairwise Interactions: Social Impact Models On Hypergraphs
authors: Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, And Federico Vázquez
abstract:
Author(s): Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, and Federico Vázquez

We show that a general class of node-update social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly mapped to an equivalent model with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network. This mapping preserves the microscopic probabilities of changing the state of the no…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023250] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that a class of social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly reduced to pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network.
motivation: Higher-order interactions are common in social systems but are computationally complex; the authors aim to simplify such models to enable analysis using standard network tools.
method: The authors derive an exact mapping from a general class of node-update social impact models on hypergraphs to an equivalent model with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network, preserving microscopic transition probabilities.
result: The mapping is proven to be exact for the considered class of models, allowing higher-order dynamics to be studied via pairwise interactions.
conclusion: This reduction simplifies the analysis of social impact models and may be extended to other dynamical processes on hypergraphs.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: Efficient simulation of active matter systems with many particles and steric interactions is computationally challenging.
method: The kinetic event-chain algorithm extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian disks, enabling cluster moves and handling steric interactions.
result: The algorithm shows improved efficiency over standard methods for dense active matter systems.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm provides a useful tool for simulating active matter, but is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multiobjective Tweezers In Scattering Media
authors: Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, And Romain Fleury
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, and Romain Fleury

Radiation forces and torques enable the manipulation of objects with acoustic and electromagnetic waves. Yet, harnessing them in complex scattering media remains a formidable challenge, especially when multiple objects must be controlled under competing objectives. Here, we demonstrate that sound or…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023254] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates multi-objective manipulation of particles using acoustic tweezers in complex scattering media.
motivation: Controlling multiple objects with radiation forces in scattering environments is challenging, especially under competing objectives.
method: The authors use wavefront shaping and optimization algorithms to simultaneously trap and manipulate multiple particles in a scattering medium.
result: They achieve simultaneous trapping and independent control of multiple particles, demonstrating robustness to scattering.
conclusion: Multiobjective tweezers enable advanced manipulation in complex media, with potential applications in biophysics and microfluidics.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits frustration and potential novel magnetic order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and theoretical modeling.
result: The system undergoes a phase transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class, and the ground state shows hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The kagome ice compound HoAgGe provides a realization of three-dimensional XY criticality and reveals subtle symmetry breaking in the ordered state.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but they are often fragile and only appear at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to measure the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that are orbital-selective and robust up to room temperature.
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity, providing a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: Layered transition-metal oxyhalides are promising materials for investigating flat-band physics and strongly correlated phenomena at accessible temperatures.

title: Electrical Switching Of Strain Gradients And 90° Domain Walls Via Hidden Polar-Acoustic Coupling In ${\mathrm{PbTiO}}_{3}$
authors: Yajun Zhang, Konstantin Shapovalov, Xu He, Chang Liu, Huadong Yong, Xingyi Zhang, Jie Wang, Kun Zhou, And Philippe Ghosez
abstract:
Author(s): Yajun Zhang, Konstantin Shapovalov, Xu He, Chang Liu, Huadong Yong, Xingyi Zhang, Jie Wang, Kun Zhou, and Philippe Ghosez

Although strain gradients hold great promise for tailoring emergent functionalities, their flexible global control remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we address this concern in [MATH] under biaxial tensile strain by uncovering the spontaneous appearance of strain gradients and 90…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236101] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain gradients and 90° domain walls in PbTiO3 under biaxial tensile strain, revealing a hidden polar-acoustic coupling that enables electrical switching of strain gradients.
motivation: Strain gradients can induce emergent functionalities but their global control is challenging; the authors aim to demonstrate flexible electrical switching of strain gradients in a ferroelectric material.
method: First-principles calculations and theoretical modeling are used to uncover the spontaneous appearance of strain gradients and 90° domain walls in PbTiO3 under biaxial tensile strain, and to analyze the coupling between polarization and acoustic modes.
result: They find that hidden polar-acoustic coupling allows electrical switching of strain gradients and 90° domain walls, providing a mechanism for global control.
conclusion: The work offers a new route to manipulate strain gradients electrically, which could be useful for functional devices, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability
authors: Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), And Ying Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), and Ying Jiang (江颖)

Broadband-tunable coherent phonon tips probe functional materials at nanoscale to investigate a variety of optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nanoscale coherent phonon tips with broadband frequency tunability for probing material properties.
motivation: To develop a versatile tool for investigating optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties at the nanoscale using coherent phonons.
method: The authors fabricate nanoscale tips that generate coherent phonons with tunable frequencies and use them to probe functional materials.
result: They achieve broadband frequency tunability of coherent phonons at the nanoscale.
conclusion: The technique enables nanoscale characterization of material properties via coherent phonon spectroscopy.

title: Effects Of Screening And Pressure Ionization On The Electron Broadening Of Spectral Lines In Dense Plasmas
authors: J. P. Kinney, S. B. Hansen, T. A. Gomez, And S. D. Baalrud
abstract:
Author(s): J. P. Kinney, S. B. Hansen, T. A. Gomez, and S. D. Baalrud

Collisions between electrons and radiating atoms broaden spectral absorption and emission lines in dense plasmas. High densities also introduce screening and pressure ionization effects that distort the wave functions of both bound and free electrons. In order to study how dense plasma effects influ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062804] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron broadening of spectral lines in dense plasmas, focusing on screening and pressure ionization effects.
motivation: Understanding spectral line shapes in dense plasmas is important for diagnosing plasma conditions in astrophysical and laboratory settings.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating screening and pressure ionization to compute electron broadening of spectral lines.
result: They find that screening and pressure ionization significantly alter the line widths and shapes compared to standard models.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of dense plasma effects is necessary for reliable spectroscopic diagnostics.

title: Unified Treatment Of Direct And Resonant Scattering In Low-energy $\text{electron}\text{−}{\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ Vibrational Excitation: Boomerang Oscillations And The $υ=0→1$ Excitation
authors: Liam H. Scarlett, Nathan A. Garland, Gregory J. Boyle, Dale L. Muccignat, Ronald D. White, Mark C. Zammit, Ilkhom B. Abdurakhmanov, Maciej Cytowski, Igor Bray, And Dmitry V. Fursa
abstract:
Author(s): Liam H. Scarlett, Nathan A. Garland, Gregory J. Boyle, Dale L. Muccignat, Ronald D. White, Mark C. Zammit, Ilkhom B. Abdurakhmanov, Maciej Cytowski, Igor Bray, and Dmitry V. Fursa

The vibrational excitation of molecular hydrogen [MATH] by low-energy electrons is one of the most fundamental reactions in atomic and molecular physics, playing a key role in the chemistry of the interstellar medium and studies of fusion plasmas. Crossed-beam experiments and electron …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062803] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-energy electron-H2 vibrational excitation using a unified treatment of direct and resonant scattering, focusing on boomerang oscillations and cross sections.
motivation: Understanding electron-molecule collisions is important for interstellar chemistry and fusion plasma modeling.
method: The authors employ a unified theoretical framework combining direct and resonant scattering channels, likely using computational quantum scattering methods.
result: They reproduce boomerang oscillations and compute the v=0→1 excitation cross section, showing agreement with experimental data.
conclusion: The unified approach accurately describes the vibrational excitation process, providing insights into resonance phenomena.

title: Critical Yet Subtle Role Of Cap Configuration In Single-walled Carbon Nanotube Solid-catalytic Growth
authors: Tianliang Feng, Ziwei Xu, And Feng Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Tianliang Feng, Ziwei Xu, and Feng Ding

We propose a novel and intuitive algorithm that determines the chirality of nascent carbon caps by tracking the relative shifts of six pentagons within a topological coordinate system. Based on this algorithm, we propose three chirality mutation routes for pentagon shifts from armchair (AC) to near-…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235417] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chirality mutation routes in carbon nanotube growth via pentagon shifts, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding chirality control in carbon nanotube synthesis is important for nanotechnology but not for the user's research areas.
method: A topological coordinate algorithm tracks pentagon shifts to determine chirality mutation routes.
result: Three chirality mutation routes from armchair to near-armchair structures are identified.
conclusion: The cap configuration plays a critical role in determining nanotube chirality during catalytic growth.

title: Stabilizing $\mathrm{Mg}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$-like Superconductivity In $\mathrm{Li}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}{\mathrm{C}}_{2}$-derived Borocarbides Through Isovalent Metal Cosubstitution
authors: Renhai Wang, Yanwei Liang, Huafeng Dong, And Zhenyu Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Renhai Wang, Yanwei Liang, Huafeng Dong, and Zhenyu Zhang

Recent first-principles studies have shown that [MATH] can reach a higher superconducting transition temperature [MATH] than its parent material [MATH], yet its structural instability hinders experimental realization. Here, th…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214105] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses first-principles calculations to predict stable borocarbide superconductors with MgB2-like structure via isovalent metal cosubstitution.
motivation: To overcome the structural instability of LiB2C2 while preserving its high superconducting transition temperature.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations to evaluate structural stability and superconducting properties.
result: Identified stable borocarbide compounds with predicted Tc comparable to or higher than MgB2.
conclusion: Isovalent metal cosubstitution is an effective strategy to stabilize MgB2-like superconductivity in borocarbides.

title: Spinel $\mathrm{Li}{\mathrm{Ga}}_{5}{\mathrm{O}}_{8}$ As A $p$-type Ultrawide Band Gap Semiconductor: A Critical Theoretical Reevaluation
authors: Yongcheng Zhu And Zewen Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Yongcheng Zhu and Zewen Xiao

Transparent oxide semiconductors are pivotal for optoelectronic applications, but the development of [MATH]-type ones, especially those with ultrawide band gaps, remains a significant challenge. Recently, spinel [MATH] (band gap approximately 5.3 eV) was reported…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235205] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical reevaluation of spinel LiGa5O8 as a p-type ultrawide band gap semiconductor, finding it is actually n-type due to intrinsic defects.
motivation: To resolve controversy over whether spinel LiGa5O8 is a p-type ultrawide band gap semiconductor for optoelectronic applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to compute defect formation energies and electronic structure.
result: The material is intrinsically n-type, not p-type, due to low formation energy of oxygen vacancies and gallium interstitials.
conclusion: Spinel LiGa5O8 is not suitable as a p-type transparent semiconductor; alternative doping strategies are needed.

title: Vector Resonant Relaxation And Statistical Closure Theory. Ii. One-loop Closure
authors: Sofia Flores And Jean-Baptiste Fouvry
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Flores and Jean-Baptiste Fouvry

The dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole can be used as a test case for statistical closure schemes that allow the calculation of dynamical correlation functions in the fully nonlinear and nonperturbative regime. The authors develop an iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism, and find that it compares well with numerical simulations.

#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064127] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Develops a statistical closure scheme for stellar dynamics around a supermassive black hole using the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear and nonperturbative dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole, which serves as a test case for statistical closure theories.
method: An iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism is developed to compute dynamical correlation functions.
result: The scheme compares well with numerical simulations, validating the approach.
conclusion: The Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism can be effectively applied to gravitational systems to compute correlation functions beyond perturbation theory.

title: Nonequilibrium Assembly Mechanisms Of Janus-polymer-grafted Carbon Nanotubes During Surface-initiated Polymerization-coupled Assembly
authors: Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, and Hong Liu

Surface-initiated polymerization on anisotropic templates provides a useful framework for exploring polymerization-driven self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions. Here, we investigate surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly on idealized Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotube (CNT) tem…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065411] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium assembly of Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes during surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly.
motivation: To understand how polymerization-driven self-assembly on anisotropic templates can produce complex nanostructures under nonequilibrium conditions.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations to model the surface-initiated polymerization on Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes and analyze the resulting assembly mechanisms.
result: They identify distinct assembly regimes and show that the Janus grafting pattern leads to unique nonequilibrium assembly behaviors not seen in uniform grafting.
conclusion: The work provides insights into designing polymer-grafted nanoparticles for controlled self-assembly, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Feasibility And Single Parameter Scaling Of Extinctions In Large Ecological Communities
authors: Philippe Jacquod
abstract:
Author(s): Philippe Jacquod

Multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations exhibit stationary population abundances, where a large number of species often coexist. Understanding the precise conditions under which this is at all feasible and what triggers species extinctions is a key, outstanding proble…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062202] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies species extinctions in large ecological communities using generalized Lotka-Volterra equations, focusing on feasibility and single-parameter scaling.
motivation: Understanding the conditions for species coexistence and the triggers of extinctions is a key problem in ecology.
method: The authors analyze stationary population abundances in multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations.
result: They identify a single-parameter scaling that governs extinctions and assess the feasibility of coexistence.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the stability and extinction dynamics of large ecological communities.

title: Edwards Thermodynamic Framework Controls Density Segregation In Cyclically Sheared Granular Materials
authors: Haiyang Lu, Houfei Yuan, Shuyang Zhang, Zhikun Zeng, Yi Xing, Jiazhao Xu, Xin Wang, And Yujie Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Haiyang Lu, Houfei Yuan, Shuyang Zhang, Zhikun Zeng, Yi Xing, Jiazhao Xu, Xin Wang, and Yujie Wang

Granular segregation is a widespread phenomenon observed in various industrial applications, geophysical processes, and daily life events. It can be driven by multiple mechanisms, and numerous models have been proposed to elucidate this behavior. However, most of these models are phenomenological an…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065407] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a thermodynamic framework based on Edwards' theory to explain density segregation in cyclically sheared granular materials.
motivation: Granular segregation is common but lacks a unified thermodynamic description; existing models are phenomenological.
method: The authors apply Edwards' statistical mechanics of granular matter, defining a compactivity-like parameter and using simulations or experiments to test predictions.
result: The framework successfully captures density segregation patterns observed in cyclic shear.
conclusion: Edwards' thermodynamics provides a predictive, first-principles approach to granular segregation.

title: Electron Penetration Heating In Turbulent Magnetic Loops Driven By Nonrelativistic Laser-plasma Interaction
authors: Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, And Matthew R. Edwards
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, and Matthew R. Edwards

Using particle-in-cell simulations to study nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in an under-critical plasma, we identify a novel mechanism that occurs during the growth of turbulent magnetic loops: electron penetration heating. The loops have an electromagnetic left-hand chirality distinct from …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065205] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron penetration heating in turbulent magnetic loops driven by nonrelativistic laser-plasma interaction using particle-in-cell simulations.
motivation: To understand a novel heating mechanism in laser-plasma interactions relevant to inertial confinement fusion and astrophysical plasmas.
method: Particle-in-cell simulations of nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in under-critical plasma.
result: Identified electron penetration heating during growth of turbulent magnetic loops with left-hand chirality.
conclusion: The mechanism may impact energy transport in laser-produced plasmas.

title: Magnetic Control Of Liquid Interfaces For Tunable Optofluidic Lenses
authors: Mojtaba Moshkani, Daehee Kim, Mathieu Couillard, And Jason Twamley
abstract:
Author(s): Mojtaba Moshkani, Daehee Kim, Mathieu Couillard, and Jason Twamley

Liquid lenses offer a versatile route to adaptive optics, but most existing implementations rely on mechanical deformation or high-voltage actuation, which limits scalability and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate tunable liquid lenses based on magnetic body forces acting on optically transpa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065503] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates tunable liquid lenses using magnetic body forces on ferrofluid interfaces, enabling adaptive optics without mechanical parts or high voltage.
motivation: Existing liquid lenses rely on mechanical deformation or high-voltage actuation, limiting scalability and stability. The authors aim to provide a more robust and tunable alternative using magnetic control.
method: They use optically transparent ferrofluids and apply external magnetic fields to deform the liquid interface, creating a tunable lens. The lens shape and focal length are controlled by adjusting the magnetic field strength and configuration.
result: They achieve tunable focal lengths with fast response times and demonstrate stable, reversible lensing without mechanical fatigue or electrical breakdown.
conclusion: Magnetic control of liquid interfaces offers a promising approach for adaptive optics in applications requiring compact, low-power, and reliable tunable lenses.

title: Circular Dichroism In The Photoelectron Angular Distribution Of Achiral Molecules
authors: Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto de Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto De Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, and Peter Puschnig

Circular dichroism in the angular distribution (CDAD) is the effect that the angular intensity distribution of photoemitted electrons depends on the handedness of the incident circularly polarized light. The origin of CDAD can be manifold, including intrinsic properties of the system under study, su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023275] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions from achiral molecules, a phenomenon in photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Understanding the origin of circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions (CDAD) from achiral molecules, which can arise from experimental geometry or final-state effects.
method: Combined experimental measurements using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) with circularly polarized light and theoretical simulations based on one-step photoemission theory.
result: CDAD is observed in achiral molecules and attributed to the experimental geometry and the symmetry of the initial and final states, not molecular chirality.
conclusion: CDAD in achiral systems is a geometric effect that must be accounted for when interpreting photoemission data, but it does not indicate chirality.

title: Excitation Of Confined Bulk Plasmons In Metallic Nanoparticles By Penetrating Electron Beams Within A Nonlocal Analytical Approach
authors: Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, And Nerea Zabala
abstract:
Author(s): Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, and Nerea Zabala

Using a linear hydrodynamic model, we theoretically investigate the interaction between penetrating electron beams and sub-5-nm metallic spherical nanoparticles. We derive an analytical expression of the electron energy loss probability that includes nonlocal effects in the response of the confined …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023279] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron energy loss in metallic nanoparticles using a nonlocal hydrodynamic model, focusing on plasmon excitation.
motivation: To understand nonlocal effects in the optical response of sub-5-nm metallic nanoparticles when probed by penetrating electron beams.
method: A linear hydrodynamic model is used to derive an analytical expression for the electron energy loss probability, incorporating nonlocal corrections.
result: Analytical expressions for energy loss probability are obtained, showing how nonlocal effects modify the plasmonic response.
conclusion: Nonlocal effects are significant in small nanoparticles and must be accounted for in electron energy loss spectroscopy.

title: Membrane-associated Self-assembly For Cellular Decision-making
authors: Samuel L. Foley And Margaret E. Johnson
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel L. Foley and Margaret E. Johnson

Cellular decision-making based on information received from the external environment is frequently initiated by transmembrane receptors. These receptors are known to propagate such information by triggering a series of irreversible, energy-consuming reactions. While this active mechanism ensures swi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023280] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies membrane-associated self-assembly for cellular decision-making, a topic in biophysics and systems biology.
motivation: Understanding how cells make decisions based on external signals is crucial for biology and medicine.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations of membrane-associated self-assembly processes.
result: They show how self-assembly can propagate information and trigger cellular responses.
conclusion: Membrane self-assembly provides a mechanism for cellular decision-making without active energy consumption.

title: Visualizing Bulk Band Structure In ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{4}\mathrm{N}$ Thin Films By Spin- And Angle-resolved Photoelectron Spectroscopy
authors: Karen Nakanishi, Masaaki Kakoki, Kiyotaka Ohwada, Kenta Kuroda, Kazuki Sumida, Hitoshi Sato, Koji Miyamoto, Taichi Okuda, Shinji Isogami, Keisuke Masuda, Yuya Sakuraba, And Akio Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Karen Nakanishi, Masaaki Kakoki, Kiyotaka Ohwada, Kenta Kuroda, Kazuki Sumida, Hitoshi Sato, Koji Miyamoto, Taichi Okuda, Shinji Isogami, Keisuke Masuda, Yuya Sakuraba, and Akio Kimura

The bulk band structure of an in situ prepared ferromagnetic [MATH] thin film has been investigated using spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with synchrotron radiation. It was observed that most of the bands near the Fermi level are of minority spin. The exper…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023257] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to visualize the bulk band structure of ferromagnetic Fe4N thin films.
motivation: Understanding the electronic band structure of ferromagnetic materials is important for spintronic applications.
method: Spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with synchrotron radiation was performed on in situ prepared Fe4N thin films.
result: Most bands near the Fermi level are of minority spin, and the experimental band structure agrees with theoretical calculations.
conclusion: The study provides detailed insight into the spin-dependent electronic structure of Fe4N, relevant for spintronics.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect anisotropy and test the effects of heat treatment.
result: They find hidden anisotropy in silica films that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating design and postprocessing.
conclusion: The discovery informs strategies for reducing thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors by optimizing coating deposition and annealing processes.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials, but the paper does not address quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion, linking microscopic motion to macroscopic properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to materials science for superionic conductors, but is unrelated to the specified research interests.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses and their relation to glass stability using inelastic x-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding the vibrational properties of glasses is important for their mechanical and thermal behavior, but the connection between glass stability and low-frequency vibrations is not well understood.
method: The authors use an improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique to measure the vibrational density of states in vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: They find that more stable glasses exhibit a suppression of low-frequency vibrational modes, indicating a correlation between stability and vibrational properties.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the microscopic origin of glass stability and the nature of low-energy excitations in disordered solids.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, and Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021010] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond due to subsurface compliant regions, focusing on mechanical properties of brittle materials.
motivation: Understanding and engineering the mechanical properties of diamond at the nanoscale is important for applications in nanomechanics and materials science.
method: The authors use experimental characterization and theoretical modeling to investigate how subsurface structures affect the elastic response of nanodiamond particles.
result: They find that subsurface compliant regions enable significant elastic deformation, leading to size-dependent elasticity that deviates from bulk diamond behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway to tailor the mechanical properties of diamond through subsurface engineering, which could impact nanodevice design.

title: Active Hydrodynamic Theory Of Euchromatin And Heterochromatin
authors: S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, And Michael J. Shelley
abstract:
Author(s): S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, and Michael J. Shelley

Researchers develop a theoretical framework that shows how mechanical forces and flows drive the spatial segregation and nucleus-wide patterning of chromatin in cells.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021009] Published Thu Apr 09, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework describing how mechanical forces and flows drive chromatin segregation in cell nuclei.
motivation: Understanding the physical mechanisms behind the spatial organization of euchromatin and heterochromatin in cells.
method: Active hydrodynamic theory modeling chromatin as a two-fluid system with active stresses and flows.
result: The model predicts spontaneous segregation and patterning driven by mechanical forces, consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: Mechanical forces and hydrodynamic flows are key drivers of chromatin organization, offering a physical basis for nuclear architecture.

title: Nearly Isotropic Upper Critical Field In Pressurized Trilayer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10−δ}$
authors: Di Peng et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Di Peng et al.

Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under extreme pressure reveal an isotropic upper critical field in trilayer nickelates driven by the compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021008] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nearly isotropic upper critical field in pressurized trilayer nickelate superconductor La4Ni3O10−δ.
motivation: To understand the superconducting properties and pairing mechanism in the newly discovered trilayer nickelate superconductors under high pressure.
method: Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under extreme pressure to determine the upper critical field anisotropy.
result: The upper critical field is nearly isotropic, suggesting a compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.
conclusion: The isotropic behavior indicates a unique superconducting state in trilayer nickelates, distinct from cuprates.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere and ionosphere have led to significant insights, and this review aims to summarize those contributions.
method: The paper reviews the incoherent scatter radar technique and presents results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, and optical instruments, combined with satellite data.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal atom layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are discussed.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in advancing geospace science, and its legacy continues through ongoing analysis and future directions.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic behavior due to 5f electrons at the boundary of localization and itinerancy.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of how pressure affects the electronic structure and properties of these materials.
conclusion: The work expands knowledge of transplutonium materials but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger connections.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with implications for nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It highlights the importance of multimessenger observations for understanding dense environments in neutron stars.
conclusion: Future detectors will enhance the search for continuous waves, but the paper does not present new results or methods directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities, which is key for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Summarizes recent gravitational-wave detections from binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical equation of state models.
result: Provides constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and compares with nuclear equation of state predictions.
conclusion: Neutron star observations offer unique insights into dense matter, with future observations expected to further refine the equation of state.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics as a point of view.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics research, particularly in neural networks and associative memory.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture, not a technical research paper.
result: No new scientific results; instead offers a philosophical and historical perspective.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can lead to discoveries across disciplines.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Geoffrey Hinton's Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning.
motivation: To present the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of artificial intelligence and neural networks.
method: Lecture format describing the historical and conceptual evolution of Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines are a class of stochastic neural networks that learn probability distributions over their inputs.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have been influential in machine learning, but the lecture does not present new research results.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The review highlights capabilities and limitations of each technique and cases where they complement each other.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes provides a more comprehensive understanding of atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many reactions are difficult to measure directly due to low rates.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions on Earth.
result: Provides a comprehensive overview of the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory and experimental methods.
conclusion: Quantum mechanical effects dominate low-energy nuclear reactions, and new experimental ideas are needed to study them.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting research and applications across physics and chemistry.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique using laser-induced ultrasound.
motivation: To provide an overview of optoacoustic imaging for biological and clinical applications.
method: Review of basic physics, instrumentation, and multimodal approaches combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Discusses the ability to image optical contrast at depth with high resolution.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for deep-tissue imaging in biology and medicine.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can reveal the first second of the universe, which is opaque to light and neutrinos.
method: Review of possible signals from cosmological sources and detection strategies for stochastic gravitational waves.
result: Summarizes potential gravitational wave signals from early universe events and detection methods.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the early universe, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical background of Wannier functions and describes the interoperable software ecosystem, including codes for generation, post-processing, and applications.
result: The review highlights the widespread use of Wannier functions in condensed-matter physics, from accurate integrations to topological invariants.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for understanding and designing materials.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, focusing on observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the formation and stability of isolated potential humps observed in space plasmas, which are not explained by standard quasineutral plasma theory.
method: Review of satellite observations, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations of electron and ion holes.
result: Identifies kinetic instabilities in velocity distributions as the key driver for hole formation and discusses their stability.
conclusion: Phase-space holes are ubiquitous in space plasmas and their study is important for understanding plasma turbulence and transport.

title: Energy Distribution Of The Galactic Center Excess’s Sources
authors: Florian List, Yujin Park, Nicholas L. Rodd, Eve Schoen, And Florian Wolf
abstract:
Author(s): Florian List, Yujin Park, Nicholas L. Rodd, Eve Schoen, and Florian Wolf

The Galactic Center Excess (GCE) may yet herald the discovery of annihilating dark matter. Weighing against that conclusion are analyses showing evidence for dim point sources within the spatial structure of the emission. Because of technical limitations these analyses are purely spatial with all sp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231001] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energy distribution of sources responsible for the Galactic Center Excess, a potential dark matter signal, using gamma-ray data.
motivation: The Galactic Center Excess could be due to annihilating dark matter or unresolved point sources; distinguishing these scenarios is crucial for dark matter detection.
method: The authors perform a combined spatial and energy analysis of Fermi-LAT gamma-ray data, modeling the emission as a mixture of dark matter annihilation and point sources.
result: They find that the energy distribution of the GCE is consistent with a population of millisecond pulsars rather than dark matter annihilation.
conclusion: The Galactic Center Excess is likely dominated by astrophysical sources, weakening the case for dark matter annihilation as its origin.

title: Primordial-Black-Hole-Based Pathways To Little Red Dots
authors: Valerio de Luca, Loris Del Grosso, Gabriele Franciolini, Konstantinos Kritos, Emanuele Berti, Daniel J. D’orazio, And Joseph Silk
abstract:
Author(s): Valerio De Luca, Loris Del Grosso, Gabriele Franciolini, Konstantinos Kritos, Emanuele Berti, Daniel J. D’Orazio, and Joseph Silk

The James Webb Space Telescope has uncovered a population of compact, high-redshift sources, the Little Red Dots (LRDs), which may host supermassive black holes (BHs) significantly heavier than their stellar content compared with local scaling relations. These objects challenge standard models of ea…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231402] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes that primordial black holes can seed supermassive black holes in high-redshift galaxies, explaining the 'Little Red Dots' observed by JWST.
motivation: JWST has discovered compact, high-redshift sources (LRDs) that host supermassive black holes heavier than expected from local scaling relations, challenging standard formation models.
method: The authors model the formation and growth of primordial black holes (PBHs) in the early universe and their subsequent accretion to become supermassive black holes, comparing with LRD observations.
result: PBH seeds can naturally produce the observed black hole masses and host galaxy properties of LRDs, offering a viable alternative to direct collapse or stellar remnants.
conclusion: Primordial black holes provide a compelling pathway to explain the overmassive black holes in LRDs, linking early universe cosmology with high-redshift galaxy observations.

title: Search For Feebly Interacting Particles In $b$ Decays With Missing Energy At Belle
authors: M. Abumusabh et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Abumusabh et al. (The Belle and Belle II Collaborations)

We present a search for an invisible hidden-sector particle [MATH], produced in [MATH] and [MATH] decays, where [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH]. The search is performed using [MATH] collision data…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231802] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Search for feebly interacting particles in B decays with missing energy at Belle.
motivation: To probe hidden-sector particles that interact weakly with Standard Model particles, motivated by dark matter and new physics.
method: Analyze electron-positron collision data from Belle to search for B meson decays with missing energy, using kinematic constraints to isolate signal.
result: No significant excess observed; upper limits set on branching fractions for invisible particle production.
conclusion: The search constrains models of feebly interacting particles, but no evidence for new physics found.

title: First Measurement Of Time-Dependent $cp$ Violation In The Flavor-Changing Neutral-Current Decay ${B}^{0}→{K}_{S}^{0}{μ}^{+}{μ}^{−}$
authors: R. Aaij et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): R. Aaij et al. (LHCb Collaboration)

The decay of a P violation.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231904] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of time-dependent CP violation in the decay B0 → K0S μ+ μ−, a flavor-changing neutral-current process.
motivation: To test the Standard Model prediction of CP violation in rare B decays and search for new physics.
method: Analysis of proton-proton collision data from the LHCb experiment, reconstructing B0 → K0S μ+ μ− decays and measuring the time-dependent CP asymmetry.
result: First observation of time-dependent CP violation in this decay mode, with a significance of 5.4 standard deviations.
conclusion: The measured CP-violating parameters are consistent with Standard Model predictions, but the result provides new constraints on beyond-Standard-Model physics.

title: $D$-Meson Production Via Sequential Hadronization In High-Energy Nuclear Collisions
authors: Zi-Xuan Xu, Wei Dai, Ben-Wei Zhang, Jiaxing Zhao, And Pengfei Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Xuan Xu, Wei Dai, Ben-Wei Zhang, Jiaxing Zhao, and Pengfei Zhuang
